title: Climbing the Ladder: The Intergenerational Mobility of Second-Generation Immigrants in France
affiliations: IÉSEG School of Management, Lille Campus, University of Lille II,  and University of Lille, LEM

detail.title: Climbing the Ladder: The Intergenerational Mobility of Second-Generation Immigrants in France
detail.abstract: We provide new evidence on intergenerational social mobility among immigrants and natives in France. Using linked parent–child data from censuses, we introduce an individual-level metric - the Intergenerational Rank Difference (IRD) - that measures upward and downward mobility relative to the highest-ranked parent across both education and predicted income. We document a robust mobility premium for second-generation immigrants: on average, they achieve a predicted income rank six percentiles higher than observationally equivalent natives, with the advantage most pronounced among women, children of two immigrant parents, and those from disadvantaged households. Educational gains explain part of this differential, but labor market advancement plays the larger role. Internal migration emerges as an important channel, as immigrant movers disproportionately relocate to high-mobility areas. Finally, a spatial analysis highlights substantial heterogeneity: some local areas act as “lands of opportunity,” while others are associated with stagnation or decline. These findings underscore the interplay of individual characteristics and local contexts in shaping long-run integration and suggest a role for place-aware policies to foster equality of opportunity.

title: Does Tipping Affect User-Generated Content Creation? Evidence from a Natural Experiment
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Notre Dame, University of Southern California - Marshall School of Business and Zhejiang University - School of Management

detail.title: Does Tipping Affect User-Generated Content Creation? Evidence from a Natural Experiment
detail.abstract: Voluntary tipping, where consumers financially reward content creators after engaging with their work, has become a widespread mechanism for incentivizing user-generated content (UGC) on digital platforms. However, its impact on content creation remains unclear because tipping differs from traditional monetary incentives in two key ways: the revenue comes from end consumers rather than platforms or advertisers, and the reward is usually based on post-consumption engagement rather than headline clicks. Does the introduction of tipping encourage creators to repeat what has worked in the past, or does it motivate them to take creative risks and produce novel content? How does it affect the volume of content produced? We investigate these questions using a natural experiment on a major Chinese blogging platform that introduced a tipping feature. Creators on this platform form the treatment group, while those on a comparable platform without tipping serve as the control group. Using coarsened exact matching and a difference-in-differences model, we find a dual effect of tipping on UGC creation: it increases content novelty measured by the degree of differentiation from both the creator’s previous work and peers’ concurrent work, but reduces content quantity measured by the number of blogs posted. The effects on content novelty and quantity are more pronounced among content creators who are more extrinsically motivated, more established on the platform, and more efficient at gaining social recognition. These findings suggest that tipping enhances novelty by aligning consumers’ demand for original content with creators’ incentives, encouraging them to prioritize novelty over volume when allocating their limited creative resources.

title: Redesigning Jobs by Automating Disfavored Tasks Benefits Workers: Field Evidence
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS) - NUS Business School and National University of Singapore (NUS)

detail.title: Redesigning Jobs by Automating Disfavored Tasks Benefits Workers: Field Evidence
detail.abstract: We investigate how automation of disfavored tasks enables the redesign of jobs to benefit workers. Conventionally, cashiers scan purchases and collect payments. A supermarket chain progressively converted stores to a scan-only checkout format which shifted the task of collecting payments to customer self-service. Vignette experiments reveal that cashiers valued the new scan-only job design at 1.5-7.3 percent of wages. The scan-only job design reduced cashiers' heart rate by 3.5 percent. Cashiers at converted stores more strongly preferred the new job design and were more risk averse as compared to those at unconverted stores.

title: From Signal to Noise: How Widespread LLM Usage Transforms Evaluator Behavior in Credit Screening
affiliations: University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Texas Tech University - Rawls College of Business, Arizona State University (ASU) - Department of Information Systems and Peking University - Guanghua School of Management

detail.title: From Signal to Noise: How Widespread LLM Usage Transforms Evaluator Behavior in Credit Screening
detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed how applicants present themselves in screening processes and has created a fundamental tension: while AI-assisted writing enables better communication of applicant quality, widespread usage may erode the informational content that evaluators rely upon for decision-making. We examine this trade-off through a randomized field experiment where 59 professional evaluators assessed 1,000 micro-loan applications, exogenously varying LLM usage rates from 0% to 75% across treatment groups. Our results reveal a non-monotonic relationship between crowd-level LLM usage and screening performance. Moderate usage rates (15-30%) improve approval outcomes for qualified borrowers without affecting default rates, while widespread usage (60-75%) generates "signal dilution," a systematic degradation in diagnostic value as stylistic homogenization reduces variance in quality indicators. Drawing on Effort-Accuracy Tradeoff Theory and Signal Detection Theory, we show that high usage rates diminish evaluators' perceived discriminatory power, prompting reduced cognitive effort and increased approval conservatism. These behavioral adaptations prove counterproductive, increasing Type I errors while failing to reduce Type II errors, ultimately worsening portfolio performance and constraining credit access. We complement our empirical findings with an analytical model that extends the analysis beyond experimental constraints, deriving optimal usage thresholds and revealing that evaluator uncertainty about LLM prevalence can paradoxically worsen screening outcomes. Our analysis establishes signal dilution and evaluator effort adjustment as key mechanisms through which AI democratization undermines decision quality in information-intensive markets, with implications for recruitment, admissions, and other high-stakes screening environments.

title: The Long-Term Effects of Air Pollution on Health and Labor Market Outcomes: Evidence from Socialist East Germany
affiliations: and Ifo Institute

detail.title: The Long-Term Effects of Air Pollution on Health and Labor Market Outcomes: Evidence from Socialist East Germany
detail.abstract: What are the long-run effects of sustained exposure to air pollution? A unique natural experiment allows us to examine this question. In 1982, a sudden cut in Soviet oil forced Socialist East Germany to switch to highly polluting lignite coal. While the shock sharply increased air pollution near mining regions, authoritarian restrictions on mobility, housing, and jobs prevented sorting responses. We document persistent labor market impacts over three decades. Exposed individuals work less, earn lower wages, and retire earlier. Health is a key mechanism: infant mortality rises by 9% and the long-run incidence of asthma and cardiopathy increases significantly.

title: From Individual Responsibility to Organizational Environment Optimization: A Paradigmatic Transition toward Post-Neoliberal Organizational Theory

detail.title: From Individual Responsibility to Organizational Environment Optimization: A Paradigmatic Transition toward Post-Neoliberal Organizational Theory

detail.abstract: This contribution introduces a significant methodological evolution in organizational theory. Through a meta-analysis of an extensive corpus of publications and based on years of applied experience, we propose overcoming approaches centered exclusively on individual performance by integrating systematic optimization of organizational environments. We present the HOWAR© Formula as a new theoretical foundation for post-neoliberal organizational science, establishing the basis for understanding human behavior through the dynamic interaction between individual identity and organizational environment. The research positions environmental quality as the primary lever for sustainable organizational performance while respecting human dignity and authenticity, proposing a paradigm shift from individual adaptation to systematic optimization.

title: Ethical hacker’s loyalties: a French case study

detail.title: Ethical hacker’s loyalties: a French case study
detail.abstract: This paper is part of an action-research project in the banking sector that was carried out between 2020 and 2023 with 30 French cyber professionals and ethical hackers. Our aim was to help companies better understand and manage ethical hackers so as to optimize their own cyber-security. For our research, we theorize about ethical hackers’ loyalty. First, we reveal the different loyalties that faces ethical hackers and complement research on loyalty. Then, we show why companies should align the contractual loyalty ethical hackers owe them with the loyalty towards the values of hackers and those of civil society at large.

title: The New Boardroom Perspective -Why We Need More Voices, Inclusivity, and AI
affiliations: Harvard University

detail.title: The New Boardroom Perspective -Why We Need More Voices, Inclusivity, and AI

declarations.ethicsApproval: Have researched and developed my own Framework for the paper

detail.abstract: The boardroom of the 21st century is facing unprecedented demands for transformation. As organizations navigate a world shaped by digital disruption, stakeholder activism, and societal shifts toward equity and sustainability, the traditional boardroom model-often exclusive, homogenous, and reactive-no longer suffices. This research paper introduces The New Boardroom Perspective, a forward-looking governance framework that integrates three essential elements: broader representation ("more voices"), genuine inclusivity, and the strategic use of artificial intelligence (AI). The paper critically examines why expanding the diversity of perspectives at the leadership levelacross gender, ethnicity, experience, and cognitive styles-is not just a moral imperative but a strategic one, directly linked to innovation, resilience, and long-term value creation. It also argues that inclusivity goes beyond numerical diversity; it requires institutional structures and cultural norms that ensure all voices are empowered to influence decisions. Furthermore, the research highlights the transformative potential of AI in the boardroom, not as a replacement for human judgment but as an augmentation tool that enhances insight, foresight, and ethical clarity. Through a multi-dimensional analysis and a detailed case study of Microsoft's inclusive AI governance model, this paper illustrates how companies can build future boardrooms that are dynamic, ethically anchored, and capable of navigating complex global challenges. By embracing The New Boardroom Perspective, organizations can move beyond legacy leadership structures and redefine governance in a way that reflects the pluralistic, digital, and data-driven world they now operate within.

title: AI-Powered System or Human Experts? Consumers’ Preference for Online Health Service under Different Frameworks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: AI-Powered System or Human Experts? Consumers’ Preference for Online Health Service under Different Frameworks
detail.abstract: AI health services are becoming increasingly important in helping users improve their overall health. However, individual attitudes and purchase preferences for human or AI health services have not been explored, which are important decision bases for healthcare providers. The proposed model synthesized the principles of rational choice theory and the framing effect, integrating the concept of perceived benefits (health outcome expectations) and perceived risks (privacy concerns and service functional risks). We conducted a scenario-based experiment containing 355 participants and confirmed the main hypotheses. The analytical results of the supplementary semi-structured interviews were consistent with the experimental findings. The research found that frameworks moderated the relationship between service provider type and purchase behavior. Consumers have higher health expectations, lower privacy concerns, and lower perceived functional risks for AI health services in the loss framework than in the gain framework, which promotes purchasing behavior. This study offers a thoroughgoing examination of consumers' behavior characteristics in regard to said services. The findings have important implications for service providers in designing more effective and tailored health services and marketing strategies.

title: Preprint Archives as Active Scholarly Communities: An Augmentation Framework
affiliations: Tongji University

detail.title: Preprint Archives as Active Scholarly Communities: An Augmentation Framework
detail.abstract: Academic conferences function as intellectual catalysts where researchers discover unexpected connections, identify complementary work, and explore new research directions through active engagement. This paper proposes a framework for preprint archives enhanced with large language models that could recreate this dynamic scholarly community while preserving researcher agency and methodological rigor. Drawing on principles of responsible LLM use and the framework of UnCritically Examined Presuppositions (UCEPs), we argue that effective AI-enhanced research infrastructure must prioritize three foundational commitments: (1) private server deployment to protect research confidentiality rather than connection to public LLM services, (2) curation of domain-specific models trained on methodologically reflective literature rather than indiscriminate scaling to maximum parameters, and (3) UCEP-aware analysis that makes visible the hidden assumptions structuring scientific inquiry. The proposed system would analyze submitted preprints across nine UCEP dimensionsincluding context dependence, fundierung dependence, quantitative indexicality, holonification, graining, clustering, communication/attention, anticipation, and memory-generating connections based on methodological alignment and productive contrast rather than mere topical similarity. By positioning AI-generated suggestions as provocations for scholarly engagement rather than authoritative recommendations, the system supports reflexive awareness while avoiding the "seductive danger of substitution" where algorithmic outputs replace critical judgment. In an era where over one million articles are published annually, this approach demonstrates that for scientific infrastructure serving confidential research, "better is better" through careful curation and contextual grounding, not "larger is better" through raw computational scale. The framework offers a model for AI-enhanced scholarly infrastructure that augments rather than replaces human expertise, maintains research ethics and confidentiality, and cultivates the second-order scientific literacy essential for maintaining intellectual autonomy in an age of pervasive AI integration.

title: Part I -Angel Investing as a Core Asset Class
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Part I -Angel Investing as a Core Asset Class
detail.abstract: This paper examines angel investing as an emerging asset class within modern portfolio construction, contrasting its risk–return profile with traditional equity and fixed income allocations. Using efficient frontier analysis, I demonstrate that incorporating venture capital or late-stage angel investments into a conventional 60/40 portfolio can meaningfully enhance expected returns and Sharpe ratios, owing to low correlations with public markets and positively skewed return distributions. The analysis draws on institutional practices—such as the Yale Endowment’s allocation to illiquid assets—as well as empirical evidence from the Kauffman Foundation and Cambridge Associates on angel and venture capital performance. Results indicate that while early-stage investing carries high failure rates and illiquidity risk, selective participation through syndicates, co-investments, or exposure to later-stage startups can improve diversification and growth potential for accredited investors. The findings suggest that angel investing, when approached with diversification and discipline, is no longer merely speculative but can function as a core component of a sophisticated investment strategy, complementing traditional assets in achieving long-term portfolio resilience.

title: Decoding Home Advantage : Empirical Insights from Premier League Data
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Decoding Home Advantage : Empirical Insights from Premier League Data
detail.abstract: This study conducts an exploratory data analysis (EDA) of English Premier League match data from the 2016/17 to 2023/24 seasons, comprising 3,040 matches and 23 variables, sourced from Football-Data.co.uk. The dataset includes match outcomes, in-game statistics (goals, shots, fouls, cards, corners), and referee information, enabling a comprehensive examination of performance trends. The analysis employs univariate, bivariate, and multivariate techniques, including histograms, boxplots, bar charts, heatmaps, decision trees, and time-series plots, to uncover patterns and relationships. Key findings highlight a significant home advantage, with home teams winning 45.3% of matches compared to 32.1% for away teams, supported by higher averages in goals (1.56 vs. 1.27), shots, and corners. The 2020/21 season, played behind closed doors due to COVID-19, shows a notable anomaly, with away teams achieving a higher win rate (40% vs. 38%), suggesting fan influence on home advantage. Referee consistency, team performance disparities and the impact of half-time states on full-time outcomes are also explored. The analysis provides insights relating to home advantage dynamics, referee influence, and tactical trends, opening pathways for further statistical modeling and sports analytics research.

title: Swamps, Springboards,  and the Demographic Dynamics  of Occupational Mobility Identifying Enablers and Inhibitors of Career Growth by Mining Education and Employment Histories  for Millions of U.S. Workers
affiliations: , Lightcast, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and Lightcast

detail.title: Swamps, Springboards,  and the Demographic Dynamics  of Occupational Mobility Identifying Enablers and Inhibitors of Career Growth by Mining Education and Employment Histories  for Millions of U.S. Workers
detail.abstract:
Understanding inhibitors and enablers for career mobility is essential for improving policy, educational programs, and economic outcomes for all labor market participants. This is especially true for individuals working in occupations below the living wage, where their personal characteristics, choice of a next job, or decision to obtain additional education can have large and often unpredictable implications for their short- and longer-term economic growth.    

In this paper, we set out to identify how specific occupational mobility choices enable or inhibit low-paid individuals’ advancement to careers that earn a living wage. By analyzing the career histories of more than 100 million individuals, we identify “springboard” occupations that launch high-earning careers and “swamp” occupations that mire workers in low-paying careers.  

Exploiting the longitudinal nature of our large dataset, we examine not only whether a worker’s next job is in a higher-paying occupation (“one-hop transition”), we also examine whether the following job is in a higher-paying occupation (“two-hop” transition). We also investigate implications of earning an educational degree for next and future occupations, as well as characteristics such as career tenure and existence of employment gaps. 

Moving from occupation to imputed demographic characteristics, we show that women and individuals of black or hispanic race experience a lower likelihood of making a springboard transition than male or white individuals, independent of occupational and career characteristics. 

We conclude by developing a policy framework to identify different interventions for swamp and springboard occupations with different growth and turnover characteristics, which we exercise with a case study of advanced manufacturing occupations.    

Our novel approach, examining short- and long-term longitudinal implications of specific career and educational choices in a dataset of more than 100 million individuals, augmented by analysis of demographic implications, provides important contributions to research on labor economics and career concerns.  Our findings can inform educators and policymakers seeking to improve career mobility outcomes for all.  They can also serve as useful inputs to help employers to address talent needs and low-paid individuals to plot a path to earning a living wage.

title: Systemic Social Problems
affiliations: United International College (UIC)

detail.title: Systemic Social Problems
detail.abstract: Any quick search on the internet or one's library catalogue can reveal that systemic social problems have not yet become mainstream, i.e. they are yet to be mainstreamed as a whole, the very most of them (cf Head, 2018). In social policy research, and social science research in general, the prevalent focus on handy choices of sealed and/or compartmentalized social problems (including economic and health problems, etc.) in the past is perhaps significantly responsible for the relative lack of higher-level systemic social problem analyses. Neither a great number of studies, nor strong or frequent research programs, on systemic social problems are visible in general social policy and social science literature. Yet, in recent years more and more studies are taking up the lead in this positive and utterly necessary direction. This is to a very large extent the outcome of media and public discourses on the subject, which once again supports the finding that social problems are identified and debated among four main actors. Either the media (including social media), the government, the experts (such as social policy scientists and practitioners) and the general public at large are pointing to, shaping and constantly reshaping social problem discourses. The same is true for systemic social problems, that either (a) talk about problems of social systems, like the economy, the education system, governance or administrative systems, or (b) talk about interrelated social problems (i.e. problem constellations of various complexity) and/or wicked problems (which require high analytical and/or remedial complexity). Both of which may require majorsystemic, paradigmatic-solutions or sets of solutions, including one or many systemic changes of all sorts. Not all wicked and/or interrelated problems are systemic problems, and not all systemic problems are wicked and/or interrelated problems. But they are to a very large extent present in the same problem or problem constellation at hand. Interrelated social problems (i.e. problem constellations) that are systemic, or wicked social problems that require systemic solutions, are yet largely under the radar or neglected in general theory making and in general social policy practice alike.

detail.title: Mobile Phones, Off-Farm Income, and Employment of Rural Women: Evidence from Bangladesh

publicationDetails.detailsText: ADB Economics Working Paper Series No. 811

detail.abstract: A persistent disparity has been observed in the social and economic development of women, particularly evident in South Asia's lower female labor force participation. This study investigates how mobile phone ownership can overcome this disadvantage. Using an instrumental variable approach and comprehensive household panel dataset from rural Bangladesh, we show that women’s mobile phone ownership is significantly associated with an increase in their off-farm income, attributable to an enhancement in the likelihood of offfarm employment. Moreover, the findings demonstrate that the adoption of mobile phones has the potential benefits being distributed equitably across various levels of education, wealth, and remoteness. The findings, as corroborated by a series of robustness checks, underscore the importance of digitalization in promoting inclusive development.

title: Enhancing Repo Market Transparency through a Quantitative Reporting Workflow
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Enhancing Repo Market Transparency through a Quantitative Reporting Workflow

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.

detail.abstract: Investors have no insight into the repurchase agreement (repo) market, the dynamics of which could have likely foreseen the 2008 Financial Crisis years sooner. Transparency into this large financial market can significantly improve market stability and price transparency of asset-backed securities. However, there have been numerous counterarguments, which include problems with market panic and institutional credit, to previous efforts for enhancing transparency for this market. This paper proposes a theoretical regulatory framework that publishes daily anonymous average haircut rate reports and implements a quantitative workflow mitigating the implications of many of the mentioned counterarguments. The workflow includes using an interpretable and auditable spike detection mechanism to identify spikes in haircut rates and withholding further haircut data, if necessary, to avoid cascading market panic; additionally, it involves using an algorithm to dynamically change the amount of lag in published haircut data to control the market's reliance, the excess of which can cause fuel for the corporate leverage effect, on published haircut data. Ultimately, this theoretical framework aims to offer a potential solution for gaining the long-anticipated transparency into this crucial financial market.

title: The use of a Stochastic Loss Given Default in a Credit Default Economic Capital Framework

detail.title: The use of a Stochastic Loss Given Default in a Credit Default Economic Capital Framework
detail.abstract: Despite the success of advanced credit portfolio models, many financial institutions still continue using a variance-covariance approach to portfolio modelling. When setting up such a framework, the parameters must be quantified and a certain number of assumptions has to be made. Assessing the level of the parameters is beyond the scope of this paper since they should ultimately pertain to peculiar features of the actual dataset. The different assumptions however should at least be mutually consistent, and a model with an inconsistent set of parameters is clearly unacceptable. We found that the concept of a stochastic loss given default in conjunction with default correlations can give rise to an inconsistent set of axioms. We propose two consistent methodologies that do not add (too much) complexity to the initial approach. These two models are also extremal in the sense that the first alternative will provide a lower bound for the variance of the portfolio loss whilst the second (comonotonic) alternative will provide an upperbound.

title: Copycats to Creators: Labubu and China's New IP Strategy

detail.title: Copycats to Creators: Labubu and China's New IP Strategy
detail.abstract: After decades of being maligned by foreigners for copying or stealing foreign IP, China and its companies are increasingly trying to emphasize innovation and domestically owned or created IP in its economy. In 2023, for example, the Chinese government announced that China would “strive to create domestic and international well known brands, improve the brand cultivation and development mechanism, and create Chinese boutique and “century-old stores.” Several Chinese companies have responded to these calls from the government to develop globally renowned brands by eschewing the non-exclusive licensing or distributing model of the past and embracing a more collaborative or innovative IP strategy while reaping the rewards of increased revenues and a higher international profile. This article highlights some prominent examples of this "new IP strategy," including Labubu/Pop Mart, Anta Sports, Mihoyo, Xiaomi, Black Myth Wukong, and the 3-Body Problem. While the specific methods in which these companies use IP differ, what they have in common is that they are highly involved in commercializing the IP not just in China but across the world, which is different from the regional distributor or licensor arrangement of Chinese firms in the past.

title: The Austerity Threshold
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University, University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School and Columbia University Graduate School of Business

detail.title: The Austerity Threshold

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no conflicts to declare.

detail.abstract: We introduce a new indicator of fiscal capacity—the "austerity threshold": the debt-to-GDP level above which the government must raise fiscal surpluses to ensure debt safety. In a model with realistic risk premia, nominal rigidities, and an intermediary sector, calibrated to the U.S., we estimate this threshold at 189%. We highlight the roles of safety premia and intermediation-driven convenience yields. The threshold varies with the source of surpluses: spending cuts reduce inflation and allow low interest rates, while tax increases distort labor supply and raise inflation. Uncertainty over the austerity regime -- spending cuts or tax increases -- sharply lowers fiscal capacity. The expected austerity regime affects asset prices and macro outcomes even when debt-to-GDP is well below the threshold.

title: Standard Axioms of the Forces of Human Coordination: A Quantum Economics Point of View
affiliations: United International College (UIC)

detail.title: Standard Axioms of the Forces of Human Coordination: A Quantum Economics Point of View
detail.abstract: Knowledge does not increase steadily, it comes in shifts (cf Kuhn, 1970a,b, 1977, 1978). Often breakthroughs have not led to shifts in knowledge and theory development/adaptation, or the paradigm changes they  demanded. Scientific knowledge is more of than not its own most vicious enemy—outdated knowledge is the worst enemy of new knowledge. Old theories, by their long-serving theorists, get (gain and maintain) permanent status and permanent powers, by way of occupying all access points (e.g. occupying reviewers’ positions in the now universally applied mechanisms of the main and exclusively acknowledged publication channels). One such case in point is old/mainstream neoclassical economics versus praxeology theory as developed by Ludwig von Mises (1940/1949), and his rejection of equilibrium economics and of utility as an untenable concept (unscientific concept) (cf Aspalter, 2025; Mises, 1978). Mises has revolutionized mainstream economics theory, but the revolution never came to be, never was allowed to unfold, roll out. Neoclassical economics of the middle-to-late 19th century still rules the heads of most current mainstream economics thinkers of today.

detail.abstract: This study examines poverty through a microeconomic lens, emphasizing household and individual behavior within resource constraints. It contrasts absolute and relative poverty definitions, highlighting their implications for consumption patterns, labor supply, and policy design. The analysis integrates monetary and non-monetary dimensions, recognizing the limitations of incomebased measures and the value of multidimensional indices. Empirical evidence from field experiments and randomized controlled trials reveals behavioral anomalies such as Giffen effects and the influence of intra-household bargaining on resource allocation, particularly regarding gender roles. Structural market imperfections, including credit access barriers and price volatility, are explored for their impact on welfare and consumption choices. The role of institutions and governance in policy implementation is assessed, noting challenges in targeting, delivery, and coordination across sectors. Advances in data collection, including Big Data and mobile technologies, offer new avenues for poverty mapping and real-time monitoring, while behavioral economics provides insights into decision-making under scarcity. The study underscores the importance of integrating quantitative and qualitative methods to capture the nuanced realities of poverty and inform adaptive, context-sensitive interventions aimed at sustainable welfare improvements.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the role of banking supervision in anticipating, monitoring, and disciplining failing banks. We document that supervisors anticipate most bank failures with a high degree of accuracy. Supervisors play an important role in requiring troubled banks to recognize losses, taking enforcement actions, and ultimately closing failing banks. To establish causality, we exploit exogenous variation in supervisory strictness during the Global Financial Crisis. Stricter supervision leads to more loss recognition, reduced dividend payouts, and an increase in the likelihood and speed of closure. Increased strictness entails a trade-off between a lower resolution cost to the FDIC and reduced credit.

title: Solvency – Liquidity Nexus Under Financial Crises: A Bidirectional Analysis of Tunisian Banks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Solvency – Liquidity Nexus Under Financial Crises: A Bidirectional Analysis of Tunisian Banks
detail.abstract: This study investigates the interaction between financial crises, bank solvency, and liquidity in the Tunisian banking sector over the period 2015- 2024, while accounting for key macroeconomic variables such as inflation and interest rates. Using a panel dataset of twelve listed banks, categorized into three types - state owned, private, and Islamic banks - and employing STATA 18 for data analysis, we explore how solvency and liquidity indicators respond to financial shocks and how these variables interact under varying macroeconomics conditions. Descriptive statistics and econometric estimations are conducted to highlight the dynamics between banks’ capital adequacy, liquidity risk, crisis episodes, and the influence of macroeconomic variables. Our findings confirm that financial crises exacerbate the solvency-liquidity nexus, amplifying banking fragility: higher solvency levels enhance banks’ resilience, while liquidity constraints and adverse macroeconomic conditions tend to amplify vulnerabilities during financial turmoil. These findings provide valuable insights for policymakers and regulators, emphasizing the importance of maintaining adequate capitalization, robust liquidity buffers, and careful monitoring of macroeconomic risks to ensure financial stability in the Tunisian banking system.

title: POI-Aware Diffusion Model for Human Mobility Prediction
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: POI-Aware Diffusion Model for Human Mobility Prediction
detail.abstract: Trajectory prediction in future urban environments remains challenging due to the complex relationship between Points of Interest (POIs) and human mobility patterns. Existing trajectory generation methods primarily rely on basic trajectory attributes that are unavailable during actual prediction scenarios, limiting their applicability to evolving cities. This research proposes a novel POI-aware diffusion model that explicitly considers spatial distributions of POIs to predict human trajectories in future urban environments. Our approach treats POI distributions as graph structures and employs a pre-trained Graph Masked Autoencoder to extract spatial embeddings, which are integrated into a conditional diffusion model for trajectory generation. Unlike previous methods, our approach uses only observable POI distributions, making it practical for real-world urban planning applications. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance across multiple distributional metrics compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of our POI embedding strategy and demonstrate the potential for efficient trajectory generation through advanced sampling techniques.The proposed method enables urban planners to predict mobility impacts of proposed developments using available environmental information, thereby supporting evidence-based decision-making in transportation infrastructure and urban development planning.

title: The Shadow Value of Central Bank Lending

detail.title: The Shadow Value of Central Bank Lending

publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
After the Great Financial Crisis, the European Central Bank (ECB) extended its monetary policy toolbox to include the use of long-term loans to banks at interest rates close to zero or even negative. These central bank interventions were aimed at supporting the transmission of expansionary monetary policy and likely played a crucial role in bolstering the financial stability of the euro area, namely by reducing the chance of bank runs. However, quantitative evidence on the effects of these interventions on financial stability remains scant. In this post, we quantify the effectiveness of central bank lending programs in supporting financial stability through the lens of a novel structural model discussed in this paper.

title: Low-light monocular depth estimation: A generative adversarial network-assisted fine-tuning approach
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology and Huazhong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Low-light monocular depth estimation: A generative adversarial network-assisted fine-tuning approach
detail.abstract: Monocular depth estimation is a fundamental task in computer vision. However, most existing methods are designed and evaluated under normal light conditions, limiting their applicability in low-light environments. In such scenarios, the lack of sufficient illumination severely degrades image quality, making it difficult for models to extract reliable features and leading to suboptimal depth predictions. To address this issue, we propose a simple yet effective approach for monocular depth estimation under low-light conditions. We first employ a Fourier-based transformation to convert normal images into low-light counterparts of the same scene, forming paired samples for training. Building upon this, we treat the encoder pretrained under normal light as a generator in an adversarial framework, and apply adversarial training to encourage the encoder to extract features from low-light images that are indistinguishable from those of normal images. We find that adversarial training alone can effectively adapt depth estimation models trained on normal images to low-light conditions. We evaluate our method on both in-domain and several unseen datasets. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements across various metrics compared to baseline, highlighting the effectiveness of our approach. These findings suggest a promising direction for achieving accurate depth estimation under challenging illumination conditions.

title: Evaluating the Impact of the national innovative city pilot policy on Green Total Factor Productivity: Evidence from China

detail.title: Evaluating the Impact of the national innovative city pilot policy on Green Total Factor Productivity: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: Guided by the concepts of economic and ecological sustainability, green development generally captures more scholarly interest, with green total factor productivity (GTFP) increasingly regarded as a critical indicator for estimating the synergy between economic advancement and ecological governance. This paper chooses China’s national innovative city pilot policy (NICPP), adopting a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) model and merging panel data from 270 prefecture-level cities between 2007 and 2022 to examine the policy’s impact on GTFP. The empirical results demonstrate that NICPP significantly promotes GTFP. The kind of effect is amplified in cities characterized by strong market potential, favorable locational conditions, sound business credit environments, and weaker foundations in traditional industry. Mechanism analysis in a further step reveals that the policy primarily affects GTFP through four channels: promoting digital financial inclusion, increasing government attention to digital technologies, optimizing urban functional division, and optimizing R&D capital allocation efficiency. These outcomes deliver empirical validation for the enhancement of GTFP and offer valuable insights for fostering economic growth in China.

title: Semantic-Aware Multi-View Person Image Generation for Re-identification
affiliations: South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, Peng Cheng Laboratory, South China University of Technology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Semantic-Aware Multi-View Person Image Generation for Re-identification
detail.abstract: Synthesizing realistic person images that preserve specific characteristics is an effective and promising approach to enhance input diversity for the re-identification (ReID) task. However, existing person image generative methods have not adequately taken into account the distribution variations of different parts of the human body across different viewpoints, resulting in the generation of unrealistic images with considerably incorrect intra-class variation. To this end, we propose a semantic-aware generative adversarial framework for high-fidelity multi-view person image generation, which provides region-level fine-grained information for person ReID. The proposed framework involves an innovative structure encoder integrating 3D information and regional parts of the person in the input sample, a group of semantic-aware generators creating intrinsic features and adaptive region weights to guide rendering, and a dual-branch generative adversarial module that synthesizes segmentation masks as supplementary supervisory information for local details of each region. Experimental results on several person ReID datasets demonstrate that the proposed method generates more realistic images with superior diversity and appearance consistency compared to existing generative models. Moreover, the proposed method significantly improves the performance of ReID methods, contributing to state-of-the-art performance.

title: Bitcoin and the Fama-French Model Rethinking Asset Pricing
affiliations: University of Exeter and

detail.title: Bitcoin and the Fama-French Model Rethinking Asset Pricing
detail.abstract: This study investigates whether cryptocurrency market risk is systematically priced in U.S. equity returns by extending the Fama–French three-factor model to include a Bitcoin-based risk factor. Using a comprehensive sample of non-financial, non-utility firms in the S&P Composite 1500, we examine how exposure to Bitcoin returns affects firm-level excess returns and whether the pricing dynamics differ between crypto-related and traditional firms. To address potential selection bias, we combine factor-model estimations with propensity score matching based on firm characteristics and sectoral affiliations. Our results reveal that incorporating Bitcoin reduces the explanatory power of the traditional value (HML) factor, suggesting that cryptocurrency risk partially subsumes conventional value effects. The Bitcoin factor is priced positively and significantly for crypto-related firms but remains insignificant for others, highlighting heterogeneity in risk transmission across firms. Robustness analyses confirm that Bitcoin acts as a diversifying risk factor exhibiting low correlation with equity returns yet offers limited downside protection during market stress. These findings extend the corporate finance literature by showing how emerging digital asset risks are integrated into firm valuation processes and by revealing the evolving structure of systematic risk in equity markets exposed to financial innovation.

title: A Self-Adaptive Genetic Algorithm for the Efficient Design of Urban Stormwater Drainage Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Self-Adaptive Genetic Algorithm for the Efficient Design of Urban Stormwater Drainage Networks
detail.abstract: Urban flooding is a major global challenge, driving the need for economically efficient stormwater drainage systems. This study develops a self-adaptive genetic algorithm (GA) for the design of stormwater drainage networks, aiming to minimize construction cost while satisfying numerous hydraulic and structural constraints. The algorithm is fully integrated with the EPA’s Storm Water Management Model (SWMM) for unsteady-flow simulation. Its core innovation is a self-adaptive penalty function that automatically manages constraints, thereby eliminating the need for manual parameter calibration, which is typically required in traditional penalty-based GAs. The model was validated using a benchmark network, achieving a lower construction cost (240,939 units) than previous studies. When applied to a real-world case study (Golsar District, Rasht, Iran), the algorithm found an optimal solution costing $23.88 million. This was 1.92% more economical and, crucially, exhibited significantly lower variance across multiple runs compared to an established adaptive GA, demonstrating superior reliability and robustness. The results confirm the algorithm's effectiveness in balancing pipe and excavation costs and its capability to utilize near-full pipe capacity without surcharge. The proposed approach offers a versatile, efficient, and parameter-free optimization tool, facilitating more reliable and economical design of urban drainage infrastructure under unsteady flow conditions.

title: Profits at Risk: The Impact of NPAs on Indian Banks' Financial Performance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Profits at Risk: The Impact of NPAs on Indian Banks' Financial Performance
detail.abstract: Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) have long posed a serious challenge to the Indian banking system, affecting both financial stability and the pace of economic growth. This paper explores the key reasons behind the rising levels of NPAs in India, including periods of economic slowdown, inadequate credit assessment, willful loan defaults, and stress in major industries such as infrastructure and power. It also highlights how the growing burden of NPAs has led to lower bank profitability, reduced investor confidence, and limited credit availability for productive sectors of the economy. In response, the study examines the recent steps taken by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the government—such as the introduction of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC)—to tackle this persistent issue. The paper concludes with recommendations aimed at strengthening asset quality and building a more resilient and trustworthy banking system in India.

title: The occurrence of microplastics in different aquatic environments of coal mining cities and the characteristics of their combined pollution with heavy metals
affiliations: Anhui University, Anhui University, Anhui University, Anhui University, Anhui Jianzhu University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Anhui University

detail.title: The occurrence of microplastics in different aquatic environments of coal mining cities and the characteristics of their combined pollution with heavy metals
detail.abstract: Microplastics (MPs), as emerging persistent pollutants, undergo complex processes of emission, migration, and accumulation within urban aquatic environments. As a major coal production base and agricultural hub in eastern China, Huaibei City is subject to multiple anthropogenic influences, including agricultural non-point source pollution, mining activities, and domestic discharges, which contribute to MPs contamination in local surface waters. This study was conducted in Huaibei City, focusing on natural rivers and lakes formed in coal mining subsidence areas. Surface water and sediment samples were systematically collected and analyzed to investigate the distribution characteristics of MPs, identify influencing factors, and assess MPs-heavy metal composite pollution across three land-use types: agricultural area (AA), mining area (MA), and residential area (RA). The results revealed that MP abundance in surface water ranged from 60 to 405 n·L⁻¹, with the highest level observed in the RA. In sediments, abundance values varied between 578 and 2857 n·kg⁻¹, peaking in the AA. Fibers represented the dominant morphotype (58.10%), and particles smaller than 0.1 mm accounted for 45.55% of all MPs. Transparent was the most prevalent color (35.63%), and the primary polymer constituents were polyethylene (PE, 43.50%) and polypropylene (PP, 36.29%). Correlation analysis indicated significant positive relationships between MPs abundance and environmental factors, including pH, total nitrogen (TN), ammonium nitrogen (NH4⁺-N), total phosphorus (TP), and sedimentary organic matter (SOM) (p < 0.05). Furthermore, concentrations of Cd, Cr, Cu, and Zn extracted from MP surfaces showed significant positive correlations with their corresponding levels in both surface water and sediments (p < 0.05), suggesting that MPs-heavy metal composite pollution may exacerbate the deterioration of water quality. These findings provide important baseline data on the occurrence characteristics of MPs in aquatic ecosystems of typical mining cities, supporting further environmental risk assessment and pollution control strategies.

title: On the Back Burner: Experimental Evidence for Energy Transitions
affiliations: , University of California, San Diego (UCSD), Duke University - Nicholas School of the Environment, Sanford School of Public Policy, Duke University  and Asian Development Bank

detail.title: On the Back Burner: Experimental Evidence for Energy Transitions
detail.abstract: A central challenge in the global transition to cleaner energy is how governments can design policies that deliver large social benefits while facing trade-offs in energy security, fiscal costs, and household adoption frictions. We study this question in urban Nepal, where cooking is dominated by imported LPG, but abundant hydropower makes both large-scale electrification and improved energy security feasible. We embed household adoption decisions in a model of a planner balancing fiscal, fuel supply, and energy-security considerations, and estimate its key parameters using a scalable randomized controlled trial in Kathmandu Valley. Subsidies had large effects, increasing electric stove adoption by 23 percentage points and compatible cookware purchases by 41 percentage points. In contrast, information treatments highlighting cost or health benefits alone had little impact. Using detailed survey and electricity billing data, we find substitution away from LPG toward electricity, with meaningful household heterogeneity. Disciplined by these experimental estimates, the model evaluates counterfactual targeting rules, and estimates optimal subsidy levels under different macroeconomic conditions.

title: Bend It like Bolsonaro: Global Evidence on the Effect of Populism on Constitutional Compliance
affiliations: University of Hamburg - Institute of Law and Economics and University of Navarra

detail.title: Bend It like Bolsonaro: Global Evidence on the Effect of Populism on Constitutional Compliance
detail.abstract: Populist governance is fundamentally at odds with constitutionalism. As a political project, populism rejects constraints on “the will of the people,” including those essential to liberal-democratic constitutions. Yet, the extent to which elected populists actually undermine constitutional order remains contested. This article presents the first empirical analysis of whether constitutional compliance declines following the electoral success of populist parties in parliament and government. Using novel indicators of party populism and constitutional compliance, we find that the entry of populists into government leads to an erosion of constitutional norms, while their mere parliamentary presence has no systematic effect. This negative impact is primarily driven by a weakening of political and civil rights. Our results further show that populist parties—as distinct from individual leaders—are the primary drivers of noncompliance, and that the ideological orientation of these parties predicts the extent of their threat to constitutional order.

detail.title: Fiscal Drag in Theory and in Practice: A European Perspective
detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive characterization of “fiscal drag”—the increase in tax revenue that occurs when nominal tax bases grow but nominal parameters of progressive tax legislation are not updated accordingly—across 21 European countries using a microsimulation approach. First, we estimate tax-to-base elasticities, showing that the progressivity built in each country’s personal income tax system induces elasticities around 1.7–2 for many countries, indicating a potential for large fiscal drag effects. We unpack these elasticities to show stark heterogeneity in their underlying mechanisms (tax brackets or tax deductions and credits), across income sources (labor, capital, self-employment, public benefits), and across the individual income distribution. Second, we extend the analysis beyond these elasticities to study fiscal drag in practice between 2019 and 2023, incorporating observed income growth and legislative changes. We quantify the actual impact of fiscal drag and the extent to which government policies have offset it, either through indexation or other reforms. Our results provide new insights into the fiscal and distributional effects of fiscal drag in Europe, as well as useful statistics for modeling public finances.

detail.title: Historical Newspaper Markets
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a novel methodology to identify the geographic market of local newspapers when information on their diffusion is not available or is not sufficiently granular. We illustrate the methodology using historical data from 154 newly digitized newspapers published in Italy between 1919 and 1922. Combining machine learning-augmented optical character recognition techniques, multi-way fixed-effect regressions, and GIS tools, our approach allows us to estimate markets based on news content. Text-based location of newspaper markets considerably improves over assuming that market boundaries coincide with administrative aggregations. We discuss how our technique strengthens the usage of newspapers as a granular and time-varying source of historical information and offers new avenues for identification strategies.

detail.abstract: We study the spillover effects of cognitive decline in one member of a coupled household on the financial outcomes of their partner and assess how "own" and spillover effects are moderated by the structure of household financial decision-making. We use a large, nationally representative longitudinal data set spanning 2000-2017 that includes credit report data merged at the individual level with Medicare claims and enrollment data. We find the own adverse financial consequences of cognitive decline depend on household financial integration and other characteristics associated with household financial management, and find significant, albeit smaller (vs own), adverse financial spillover effects on partners.

detail.abstract:
Korean Abstract:
기후위기 대응에 대한 국제사회의 요구가 높아지는 가운데, 온실가스를 감축하면서 경제적 수익을 창출하는 기후테크는 탄소중립 전환의 핵심요소로 부상하였다. 본 연구는 우리나라 기후테크 혁신성과를 분석하고, 글로벌 「선두 개척자」(first mover)로의 도약을 저해하는 주요 과제를 규명한다.

본 연구는 2011~21년 미국 특허청(USPTO)에 등록된 특허 데이터를 활용하여 주요국과 우리나라의 기후테크 혁신성과를 비교 분석하였다. 양적 지표(특허출원건수)와 질적 지표(후속파급력, 창의성, 범용성, 급진성)를 활용하여 재생에너지, 2차전지, 전기차, ICT, 탄소포집·활용·저장(CCUS), 화학·정유·철강 등 탄소집약산업 기술 등 주요 기후테크 분야의 혁신성과를 평가하였다.

분석 결과, 우리나라는 양적으로는 양호한 모습을 보였다. 특허출원건수가 세계 3위를 기록하였으며, 다른 선도국이 2010년대 중반 이후 정체된 반면 우리나라는 꾸준한 증가세를 유지하였다. 그러나 우리나라 기후테크 특허의 2/3 이상이 4개 기업과 4개 기술분야(2차전지, 전기차, 재생에너지, ICT)에 집중되었다. 더욱이 우리나라는 양적으로 우수한 성과를 보이는 분야에서조차 대부분의 질적 특허평가지표에서 10대 선도국 중 하위권에 머물렀다.

본 연구는 이러한 문제의 원인을 세 가지로 규명하였다. 첫째, 한국 기업은 중장기적 혁신 필요성보다 단기 수익을 우선시하여 상용화 단계 기술(2022년 기업 기후테크 R&D 지출의 65%)에 집중하는 반면, CCUS(1%)와 기초연구는 소홀히 하고 있다. 둘째, 정부의 R&D 지원과 탄소가격 정책이 장기적 기후테크 혁신에 충분한 유인을 제공하지 못하고 있다. 저탄소에너지기술에 대한 정부 R&D 투자 비중은 2021년 2.9%로 중국 제외 10대 선도국 중 최하위였으며, 유효탄소가격은 2023년 26.0유로/tCO2로 선도국 평균(64.7유로/tCO2) 대비 크게 낮은 수준이었다. 셋째, 기후테크 혁신자금 조달여건이 취약하다. 2016~23년 녹색채권 발행(GDP 대비 0.3%)과 기후테크 벤처캐피탈 투자(GDP 대비 0.003%)는 다른 선도국 평균을 크게 하회하였다.

이러한 문제를 극복하고 기후테크의 「선두 개척자」로 도약하기 위해, 본 연구는 세 가지 정책 방향을 제시한다. 첫째, 정부 R&D 지원을 강화하여 탄소저감기술로의 「유도된 혁신」을 촉진해야 한다. 특히 탄소집약산업과 CCUS에 대한 지원을 확대해야 한다. 둘째, 탄소가격제의 실효성을 제고하여 탄소배출기술에서 탄소저감기술로 「왜곡된 혁신」을 전환해야 한다. 나아가, 탄소가격제에서 거둔 수입은 저탄소기술 R&D 자금으로 환류되도록 설계해야 한다. 셋째, 투자회수시장 확대, 정부벤처캐피탈 강화, 공공 인내자본 제공 등을 통해 벤처캐피탈 투자를 활성화하여 기업이 「죽음의 계곡」을 건너갈 수 있도록 혁신자금 조달여건을 개선해야 한다.

본 연구의 OECD 회원국 실증 분석에 따르면, 이 세 가지 정책을 효과적으로 시행할 경우(정부 R&D 지원, 탄소가격, 벤처캐피탈 투자를 각각 40% 확대) 우리나라의 혁신의 양과 질을 모두 반영한 기후테크 혁신성과가 최상위국 수준에 이르는 것으로 나타났다. 이는 통합적 정책 추진을 통해 우리나라가 기후테크 분야에서 「선두 개척자」로 도약할 가능성을 시사하며, 기후변화 대응과 탄소중립경제로의 전환에서 경쟁력 강화에 기여할 수 있음을 보여준다.

English Abstract:
Amid growing international calls to address the climate crisis, climate technology, which reduces greenhouse gases while generating economic benefits, has emerged as a key element in the transition to carbon neutrality. This study analyzes Korea's climate technology innovation performance and identifies key challenges hindering Korea's leap forward as a global "first mover."

Using patent data registered with the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) from 2011 to 2021, this study compared and analyzed the climate technology innovation performance of Korea with that of major countries. Using quantitative indicators (number of patent applications) and qualitative indicators (follow-up impact, creativity, versatility, and radicality), the study assessed innovation performance in key climate technology sectors, including renewable energy, secondary batteries, electric vehicles, ICT, carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS), and technologies for carbon-intensive industries such as chemicals, refining, and steel.

The analysis results show that Korea performed well quantitatively. Korea ranked third globally in the number of patent applications, and while other leading countries have stagnated since the mid-2010s, Korea has maintained a steady increase. However, more than two-thirds of Korea's climate technology patents are concentrated in four companies and four technology fields (secondary batteries, electric vehicles, renewable energy, and ICT). Furthermore, even in fields where Korea exhibits quantitative excellence, Korea ranks low among the top ten leading countries in most qualitative patent evaluation indicators.

This study identifies three causes of this problem. First, Korean companies prioritize short-term profits over mid- to long-term innovation needs, focusing on commercialization-stage technologies (65% of corporate climate technology R&D spending in 2022), while neglecting CCUS (1%) and basic research. Second, government R&D support and carbon pricing policies fail to provide sufficient incentives for long-term climate technology innovation. Government R&D investment in low-carbon energy technologies stood at 2.9% in 2021, the lowest among the top ten leading countries excluding China. The effective carbon price, at €26.0/tCO2 in 2023, was significantly lower than the leading country average (€64.7/tCO2). Third, financing conditions for climate tech innovation are weak. Between 2016 and 2023, green bond issuance (0.3% of GDP) and climate tech venture capital investment (0.003% of GDP) significantly fell below the averages of other leading countries.

To overcome these challenges and leap forward as a "leading pioneer" in climate tech, this study proposes three policy directions. First, government R&D support should be strengthened to promote "directed innovation" in carbon reduction technologies. In particular, support for carbon-intensive industries and CCUS should be expanded. Second, the effectiveness of the carbon pricing system must be enhanced to shift "distorted innovation" from carbon-emitting technologies to carbon-reducing technologies. Furthermore, revenues from the carbon pricing system must be designed to be circulated back into low-carbon technology R&D funding. Third, by stimulating venture capital investment through expansion of the investment recovery market, strengthening government venture capital, and providing public patient capital, we must improve the conditions for innovation financing to help companies overcome the "valley of death."

According to this study's empirical analysis of OECD member countries, effective implementation of these three policies (increasing government R&D support, carbon pricing, and venture capital investment by 40% each) would lead to Korea achieving top-tier climate technology innovation performance, reflecting both the quantity and quality of innovation. This suggests the potential for Korea to become a "leading pioneer" in climate technology through integrated policy implementation, contributing to enhanced competitiveness in responding to climate change and transitioning to a carbon-neutral economy.

detail.title: The Role of Fairness Ideals in Coordination Failure and Success
detail.abstract: In a laboratory experiment, we study the role of fairness ideals as focal points in coordination problems in homogeneous and heterogeneous groups. We elicit the normatively preferred behavior about how a subsequent coordination game should be played. In homogeneous groups, people share a unique fairness ideal how to solve the coordination problem, whereas in heterogeneous groups, multiple conflicting fairness ideals prevail. In the coordination game, homogeneous groups are significantly more likely than their heterogeneous counterparts to sustain efficient coordination. The reason is that homogeneous groups coordinate on the unique fairness ideal, whereas heterogeneous groups disagree on the fairness ideal to be played. In both types of groups, equilibria consistent with fairness ideals are most stable. Hence, the difference in coordination success between homogeneous and heterogeneous groups occurs because of the normative disagreement in the latter types of group, making it much harder to reach an equilibrium at a fairness ideal.

title: Civilizational Scaffolding Entropy: A Mathematical Framework for Systemic Collapse

detail.title: Civilizational Scaffolding Entropy: A Mathematical Framework for Systemic Collapse
detail.abstract: We define civilizational scaffolding as the system-level supporting structure that sustains human life and social order. We treat civilization as a coupled system of five load-bearing domains: ecology, culture, technology, economy, and politics. We introduce scaffolding entropy: a named family of normalized disorder measures within each domain, paired with a coupling map and thresholds to trace how strain spreads. Two routes to failure emerge: tighter ties or slower recovery shrink the stability margin so small shocks travel farther; and threshold breaches accelerate contagion along links. The framework yields an early-warning dashboard: slowing recoveries, a single stability margin independent of units and threshold choices, and two threshold-aware gauges for progress to breach and remaining headroom. We use the spectral check as a sufficient early-warning test under a stated normalization. Policy follows: changing domain weights only re-averages stress and cannot move the stability boundary, while adjusting couplings or recovery rates can. Targeted decoupling or faster recovery restores safety with limited performance loss. In a 2008 case study, a smoothed stability indicator entered its warning zone in 2006 over two years before the Lehman collapse, illustrating a transparent, testable toolkit to monitor systemic fragility and guide policy within the stability boundary.

2. פרק ב׳ מהווה נרטיב מקביל המתאר את הכרונולוגיה הפיזית של יצירת העולם והאדם ("יהוה אלוהים"), וחושף תאימות נשגבת לרצף האבולוציוני: מעולם של אדמה ומים, דרך המחזור ההידרולוגי וצמיחת הצומח, ועד יצירת ה״אדם״ כ ״נפש חיה״ (יונקים/חיים מוקדמים).

על בסיס הפרשנות הכפולה, המאמר מראה כיצד העולם המדעי מפספס את החיבור הקריטי הזה בשל הקריאה השגויה של פרק א' כרצף פיזי. פרקים ב' ו-ג' מתוארים כשיאו של התהליך: תיאור ההתגלמות הפיזית של התודעה (כתנות עור) וכינון האדם כישות מודעת באמצעות השגת ה ״דעת טוב ורע״. בניתוח זה, מוצעת פרספקטיבה תיאולוגית-פסיכולוגית חדשנית, המציבה את הכתובים כמקור לגיטימציה תיאולוגית לתהליכים האבולוציוניים, ובכך מאפשרת לאחוז יחד בנרטיב הרוחני המכונן ובמציאות המדעית-האבולוציונית של קיום האדם.

Abstract

This article proposes a revised and systematic reading of the Creation Story in the Book of Genesis (Chapters 1–3), seeking to bridge the historical gap between the traditional religious narrative and scientific/evolutionary findings. The central thesis posits that the Creation Story is divided into two distinct and parallel narratives: 1. Chapter 1 is not a chrono-physical description, but an allegory for the development of collective human consciousness ("Elohim")—from the moment of awakening out of the "Tohu V'Vohu" (chaos) to the fundamental ability to perceive and make basic distinctions (light/dark, land/sea). 2. Chapter 2 serves as a parallel narrative describing the physical chronology of the creation of the world and man ("YHWH Elohim"), revealing a sublime compatibility with the scientific evolutionary sequence: from a world of land and water, through the hydrological cycle and the emergence of flora, and finally to the creation of 'Adam' as a 'living soul' (early life/mammals). Based on this dual interpretation, the article demonstrates how the scientific world misses this critical connection due to the flawed reading of Chapter 1 as a physical sequence. Chapters 2 and 3 are depicted as the culmination of the process: the description of the physical embodiment of consciousness (the 'garments of skin') and the establishment of man as a conscious entity through the attainment of 'the knowledge of good and evil'. This analysis offers a novel theological-psychological perspective, positioning the Scriptures as a source of theological legitimation for evolutionary processes, thereby allowing the spiritual narrative and the scientific-evolutionary reality of human existence to be held in harmony.

detail.abstract: The Blended Retirement System introduces new retention incentives across all services, but its impact on service members remained largely unexplored. This study is the first to rigorously estimate the Blended Retirement System’s effect on retention. In this study, I analyze ten years of Marine Corps panel data, focusing on the 2017 and 2018 cohorts, using a regression discontinuity design and complementing it with a linear probability model for robustness. I find that Marines in the Blended Retirement System separate at rates 5.2 to 7.6 percentage points lower than those on the Legacy Plan, indicating that prior projections failed to capture how service members value immediate over deferred benefits fully. This discovery presents a dual challenge for policymakers: they must balance rising federal expenditures on the military retirement system while addressing persistent personnel shortages.

title: Thematic Meta Analysis in Social Policy Science
affiliations: United International College (UIC)

detail.title: Thematic Meta Analysis in Social Policy Science
detail.abstract: Each scientific discipline has to build and develop further discipline-specific methodology; i.e. to focus on, use and develop unique sets of methods that are designed to, or simply happen to, bring about progress in knowledge creation and deepening, as well as critical evaluations thereof. Social policy science is dealing with all sorts of problems that are mostly shared by countries, societies, communities all over the world, with at times great differences, and sometimes not. Social policy is also home to multi-layered, Lasagna-style social problems or societal problems, and scientific problems (in general) as well. Wicked causalities, wicked interactions, wicked hidden truths and hidden pasts, hidden side effects, hidden follow-on effects, all contribute to the need to upgrade analytical methodology. The word 'meta', in meta analysis, comes from Greek language and stands mostly for 'beyond,' i.e. beyond the usual, beyond the normal. Some studies are conceptualized at greater level-some abstract level, some global level, some grand-ourstorical(grand-historical) level, some try to tackle multilayered/multicyclical causalities, some are just so wide that they cover many more topics and themes in themselves, by themselves. These are all meta studies, using the method of (non-statistical) meta analysis, which here is understood as a social-policyscience-specific method (Aspalter, 2021). This has nothing to do with marketing, psychology, or medical science, etc., where different kinds of statistical meta analyses are applied, focusing on merging data and findings of other (a great, greater number of) studies. To be sure in social policy science, non-statistical meta analyses are very common, and super influential in bringing about progress, exploration, understanding and solutions (Aspalter, 2021). Grand themes, i.e. meta thematic analyses, are actually the main or most frequent choice of a great deal of social policy scientists.

detail.title: Public Service Delivery Shortages and Governance in Salah al-Din, Iraq A Comparative Perspective
detail.abstract: This paper examines the shortages in public service delivery in Salah al-Din governorate, Iraq, focusing on the health, drinking water and sanitation, municipal, education and other sectors. It situates these shortages within Iraq's broader governance challenges, marked by entrenched corruption, weak decentralization, political fragmentation, and conflict legacies. Drawing on reports from the International Organization for Migration (IOM), UNDP, Chatham House, the World Bank, and national policy briefs, the analysis provides both national-level and local-level insights. The study highlights concrete cases in Salah al-Din such as the long-delayed Mkeishifa Bridge in Samarra, the neglected neighborhoods outside Tikrit's master plan, the dire state of Hemrin's schools, and tribal and sectarian bias in service distribution. Comparisons with Ninewa, Anbar, Basra, and the Kurdistan Region further illustrate the governance-driven disparities. Recommendations emphasize ministry-led capacity development focused on technical staff, unifying digitizing procedures, strengthening feedback and inclusion, promoting equity, enhancing local ownership, and integrating housing with service restoration-building a transparent, citizen-centered, and resilient governance system in Salah al-Din.

detail.title: Dynamics of GDP, Consumption, and Per Capita Income in Pakistan: Evidence from the PWT 10.01 (1950–2019)
detail.abstract:
This study takes a close look at Pakistan’s economic growth over a long period, from 1950 to 2019, using trusted data from the Penn World Table. It examines important factors such as real GDP (measured by spending and production), consumption, and population, and how these shape income per person. Statistical tests confirmed that these economic variables are linked in a stable, long-term way, which allowed the use of a specialized model called the Vector Error Correction Model (VECM).

The findings show that when GDP from spending increases, it positively impacts production, consumption, and income levels, pointing to growth driven by demand. Interestingly, increases in consumption at constant prices do not always translate to more growth or better welfare, suggesting some structural issues, such as too much reliance on imports and weak investment.

Overall, Pakistan’s growth seems to depend significantly on aggregate spending, but lasting progress requires boosting investment and exports, improving fiscal management, and focusing on human capital development to ensure that higher incomes reach more people sustainably.

detail.title: The Path to a Carbon Neutral Economy: Current Status and Challenges of Korea's Climate Technologies

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Korea III. In-depth Analysis

detail.abstract:
As global demands for addressing the climate crisis intensify, climate technologies—innovations that reduce greenhouse gases while generating economic returns—have become essential for the transition to carbon neutrality. This paper examines Korea's climate technology innovation performance and identifies key challenges hindering its advancement as a global leader in this critical sector.

Using patent data from the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) for 2011-2021, we conduct a comprehensive analysis comparing Korea's climate technology innovation performance with major countries. We employ both quantitative metrics (patent application counts) and qualitative indicators (forward citations, originality, generality, and radicalness) to assess innovation performance across various climate technology sectors including renewable energy, batteries, electric vehicles, ICT, carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS), and technologies for carbon-intensive industries such as chemical, oil refining, and steel.

Our analysis reveals a paradox in Korea's climate technology landscape. Quantitatively, Korea ranks third globally in climate technology patent applications and has maintained steady growth while other leading nations have stagnated since the mid-2010s. However, more than two-thirds of Korea's climate technology patents are concentrated in four companies and four technology areas (secondary batteries, electric vehicles, renewable energy, and ICT). Furthermore, Korea demonstrates insufficient qualitative performance, remaining in the lower ranks among top-10 countries in originality, generality, and radicalness indicators, even in sectors where it shows strong quantitative performance.

We identify three primary causes of these challenges. First, Korean firms prioritize short-term returns over long-term innovation needs, concentrating R&D investments in commercialized technologies (65% of corporate climate tech R&D in 2022) while neglecting critical areas like CCUS (only 1%) and basic research. Second, government policies provide insufficient incentives for long-term climate technology innovation: Korea's R&D investment share in low-carbon energy technologies (2.9% in 2021) is the lowest among top-10 countries excluding China, and its effective carbon price (€26.0/tCO2 in 2023) falls below the peer average (€64.7/tCO2). Third, innovation financing conditions remain weak, with green bond issuance (0.3% of GDP, 2016-2023) and venture capital investment in climate tech (0.003% of GDP) substantially below other leading countries.

To overcome these issues and advance as a "first mover" in climate technology, we propose three policy directions. First, strengthen government R&D support to promote "induced innovation" toward carbon reduction technologies, particularly for carbon-intensive industries and CCUS. Second, enhance carbon pricing effectiveness to shift "distorted innovation" from carbon-emitting to carbon-reducing technologies, while recycling revenues into low-carbon R&D funding. Third, expand innovation financing by activating venture capital investment through secondary market development, government venture capital, and public patient capital provision to help firms cross the "valley of death."

Our empirical analysis of OECD member countries demonstrates that if these three policies are effectively implemented—specifically, if government R&D support, carbon prices, and venture capital investment each increase by 40%—Korea's citation-weighted patent performance could reach the levels of top-performing countries. This finding suggests the feasibility of Korea becoming a "first mover" in climate technology through coordinated policy action, with implications for both climate change mitigation and economic competitiveness in the emerging green economy.

detail.abstract: This report investigates the structural dynamics and long-run behaviour of Danish inflation, focusing on the interrelationship between total and core inflation from 1985Q1 to 2025Q4. Using a combination of Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) tests, Engle-Granger and Johansen cointegration approaches, and Vector Error Correction Modelling (VECM), the analysis provides strong empirical evidence of cointegration between total and core inflation, indicating a stable long-run equilibrium. Structural break tests, including the Newey-West regression and Supremum Wald methodology, reveal statistically significant regime shifts-most notably around 2021Q2corresponding to post-pandemic price realignments and global supply disruptions. Forecasting is conducted through both direct and iterative approaches, with the direct VECM method yielding superior robustness against structural breaks and error propagation. The resulting forecasts suggest a gradual decline in both total and core inflation over the subsequent four quarters, supported by easing commodity prices, stabilising monetary policy and a cooling labour market. Despite these downwards trends, widening forecast intervals underscore persistent uncertainty linked to global economic volatility and trade dependencies. The findings carry critical implications for monetary policy in Denmark. A flexible policy stance-aligned with European Central Bank dynamics-is recommended to balance inflation control with sustainable economic growth. In summation, this report contributes to the understanding of inflationary persistence, structural shifts and the predictive performance of cointegrated econometric models within small open economies.
