detail.abstract: Chevron deference is neither a standard nor a tool of interpretation. Rather, it is a description of presumed congressional delegation of legislative decision-making authority and a framework for evaluating the consequences of such presumed delegation. So understood, the relation between Chevron deference, the rule of lenity, and how to address an executive agency’s failure to exercise delegated legislative authority becomes simple to resolve. Implied delegations of legislative authority are suspect, particularly where the premise of such implication is a congressional failure to use clear statutory language, thus requiring legislative policy decisions by the executive branch. Such suspicion should become prohibitive where a statute bearing criminal penalties is involved. Separation of powers precludes executive definition of crimes. Even were such a delegation in the criminal or mixed context were permissible, the failure or refusal affirmatively to exercise delegated discretion would eliminate the premise for Chevron deference.

detail.title: Taxing AI Across Borders: The Benefits of In-Kind Remittance for Cross-Border Taxation
detail.abstract:
The five largest companies in the world, as measured by market capitalization, are all U.S. Artificial Intelligence ("AI") companies. Although incorporated in the U.S., the activities of these firms are global. Indeed, the profit model for many of these AI companies is to decimate the labor markets of foreign economies by substituting the domestic labor of target markets with foreign-sourced AI. Much of this AI was also trained on data stolen from foreign jurisdictions. The cross-border ownership of AI, the cross-border labor market impact of AI, and the crossborder profit flows of AI all place substantial pressure on the international tax system. In response to these challenges, this essay explores a new approach to taxing AI firms that would require payment in equity rather than cash. Extending prior research proposing fractional public ownership of generative AI firms under U.S. law (Bearer-Friend & Polcz, 2025), this essay applies an original AI tax proposal to the international context. Non-U.S. jurisdictions could require a one-time payment of equity in order to sell AI services to customers within their respective countries. Beyond the immediate implications for taxing AI across borders, this essay also challenges a broader assumption in tax scholarship. The tacit presumption that taxes should only be paid in cash rather than other forms of property undermines the efficacy of taxation generally and cross-border taxation particularly.

title: From Socialism to Markets

detail.title: From Socialism to Markets

detail.abstract: How did the early egalitarian or socialist views of James Buchanan, Ronald H. Coase, Aaron Director, Milton Friedman, F. A. Hayek, Wilhelm Röpke, and Walter Lippmann evolve into a rejection of collectivism? While these scholars and economic writers are regarded as key defenders of free markets, before engaging with economics, each harbored egalitarian or socialist sympathies. Drawing on biographical accounts and early writings, we trace their initial inclinations toward interventionism and collectivism and their eventual rejection of these views. Far from being driven by ideology, their journeys reflect a shared scholarly readiness to discard unsupported beliefs when confronted with compelling theoretical and empirical evidence. Their intellectual paths underscore the pivotal role economic training can play in placing constraints on worldviews. However, not all economic education is effective. Early exposure to technical economics was uninfluential for Buchanan, Friedman, Hayek, and Lippmann. Examining the teaching methods of Knight, who influenced 4 of the economists reviewed in this paper, we argue it was exposure to the coordinative dynamics of the market process that transformed their views.

title: The Interplay between Different Streams of Social Policy Theory
affiliations: United International College (UIC)

detail.title: The Interplay between Different Streams of Social Policy Theory
detail.abstract: A very good description of the problems of the interplay between different streams of social policy theory is given by Modood and Favell (2003), as well as Bauböck (2008). They discussed the key problems that arise from e.g., as in a (shockingly) large number of cases, working on social policy description (case studies, thematic papers, historical/ourstorical papers, etc.) and casually adding normative lessons or suggestions. Or conducting blindly descriptive social policy research projects or research works without knowing (as in most cases, as there are barely social policy-own normative theories), or not understanding normative social policy theory (having not fully read them, as so often, or simply not having gotten the gist of things, or not yet). Also, running evaluations and prescriptions (normativity-based social policy research projects and research studies) without fully knowing the empirical reality on the ground, is a monster-sized problem in social policy science, as most studies and books concentrate only on a very small number of countries (and that among Western countries). Global multicenter case studies are yet super seldom, and they themselves represent a very good starting point in analyzing and conquering (intellectually, and scientifically that is) the whole world-with all the people in it, in all countries, in all corners (on all plains, in all valleys, on all mountains, on all islands)-within the realm and discipline of social policy. Medical science and the field of health policy is a head of social policy science in applying multicenter social policy analyses. If one looks for it there are a larger number of multicenter case studies in social policy, but they are only a tiny fraction of all case studies, and yet not fully noticed, with their great value not yet fully appreciated far and wide. The great usefulness of such studies is shown e.g. by Wong and Ho (2023) when analyzing the impact and response measures to the Covid-19 Pandemic in several cities around the world, going both deep and wide, as is the winning formula of multicenter case study analysis. Quantitative global local data analysis is the next step up after ordinary global data analysis. In abolishing the container view of looking at nation states, we in social policy science in particular need to focus on (global) local data, not on national-aggregated, averaged(!)-data. Schumpeter (1951) knew about the problems of science based on (scientifically random, meaningless, fully obscuring) national boundaries and their aggregates. Social policy science needs to follow this imperative.

detail.title: Brief of Amici Curiae in Support of Petitioner; Caniglia v. Strom, 593 U.S. 194 (2021).
detail.abstract:
The sanctity of the home is central to American freedom. It has been central to the idea of freedom since the Roman Republic, and it was cherished by Englishmen for centuries leading up to the American Revolution. 

Embodied in the Castle Doctrine, the inviolability of the home was celebrated by leading English legal authorities, including Edward Coke, William Hawkins, and William Blackstone. As William Pitt the Elder famously declared, even the poorest soul in the country had the right to defy the king in his own home. 

But the English government nevertheless violated the sanctity of the home to seize property and to suppress speech, religion, assembly, political opposition, and firearm ownership. The English constantly complained about such infringements, but the violations continued.

American colonists, by contrast, had no tolerance for home intrusions. Violations of the home often resulted in hostility. Eventually, the colonial response to abusive home intrusions became so violent that even many lawful searches could not be conducted.

American resistance to home invasions ultimately led to the American Revolution. According to John Adams, when James Otis delivered his fiery speech against writs of assistance, American independence was born. 

Many debates over the United States Constitution and the Bill of Rights focused on the need for robust and explicit protections for the home. Ultimately, the home became central to the Bill of Rights. The First through Fifth Amendments collectively create a zone of safety and protection in the home. Thus, the home has remained every American’s castle throughout all of American history. 

The decision below, however, permits home intrusions whenever the officer acts “within the realm of reason” while executing community caretaking responsibilities. Such a standard would allow many of the home intrusions the founders vehemently opposed. Indeed, extending the community caretaking exception to the home would undermine the constitutional text, the founders' intent, and centuries of tradition.

detail.title: Beyond Rules: The Dreck Equation for Quantifying Unseen Federal Regulatory Burdens
detail.abstract: This brief paper introduces the Dreck Equation, a conceptual framework for envisioning the full scope of federal regulatory intervention beyond conventional notice-and-comment rulemaking. Inspired by Frank Drake's famous probabilistic Drake Equation for the presence of extraterrestrial life, the Dreck Equation combines observable notice-and-comment rulemaking with unobserved or less visible "rule equivalents"-including guidance documents, memoranda, administrative interpretations, procurement conditions, subsidies, and public-private partnerships-that function as regulatory dark matter, potentially outweighing the published and visible. While the Federal Register chronicles roughly 3,000 rules annually, the effective burden on enterprise and civil society is vastly larger and unmeasured. By proposing the development and quantification of a "Dreck Load" encompassing both visible and hidden interventions, this paper calls for a comprehensive accounting of the administrative state's reach and highlights the need for congressional, executive and judicial reforms to reduce the gravitational pull of extrastatutory administration.

title: Cracking AI Secrecy: EU Migration Law & Governance and Beyond

detail.title: Cracking AI Secrecy: EU Migration Law & Governance and Beyond
detail.abstract: In core government and for public tasks hugely sensitive for citizens such as migration governance in Europe, the use of AI systems developed and provided under contract gives migration authorities and private providers the power to keep their deployment secret and to refuse access to their key components. This paper explores the complex interplay between public and private drivers of secrecy surrounding procured AI technologies in European migration governance, demonstrating how these forces converge and reinforce one another. We examine AI secrecy as an institutional framework shaped by both public and private law forms of secrecy, applying the spectrum of secrecy from deep (unknown unknowns) to shallow secrecy (known unknowns). Specifically, our paper delves into the sources of ‘political secrecy’ in migration and security authorities, highlighting how migration agencies and authorities keep the existence and use of AI systems from the civil society and affected persons (such as third country nationals). Next, it analyses the legal frameworks that sustain AI vendors’ private secrecy, such as trade secrecy, secrecy in procurement procedures and agreements. In examining the various secrecy points, the paper critiques the limited impact of the newly enacted AI Act in addressing the entrenched secrecy of AI deployment and development in migration governance. Finally, we condense the main takeaways and examine the broader repercussions of AI secrecy beyond the context of migration governance, touching upon its implications for a new equilibrium transcending the conventional public/private divide.

title: An Analysis of Monetary Policy Evidence and Theory through Meta-Analyses

detail.title: An Analysis of Monetary Policy Evidence and Theory through Meta-Analyses
detail.abstract: This paper offers a synthesis of the empirical literature on the effects of monetary policy. Using the findings from an extensive collection of meta-analyses, it evaluates the effectiveness of conventional and unconventional monetary policy instruments on key macroeconomic variables such as output, inflation, capital flows, and the exchange rate. The aggregated evidence reveals a systematic gap between the effects reported in primary studies and the actual magnitude of these effects, once corrected for publication bias and methodological heterogeneity. The findings suggest that, while monetary policy is a relevant tool, its power to modulate the business cycle has been consistently overestimated in the literature. Contextual factors-such as the degree of financial development, the exchange rate regime, central bank independence, and crisis conditions-that modulate the transmission of monetary policy are identified. In particular, it is found that publication bias systematically favors statistically significant results consistent with predominant theory, which artificially inflates the perception of effectiveness. By correcting these distortions, a picture of monetary policy emerges with more modest, uncertain effects and considerable lags, which has profound implications for macroeconomic theory and the practice of economic policy.

detail.title: Directed R2 Connectedness Measures
detail.abstract: The R 2 connectedness approach proposed by Naeem et al. 2024 has gained attention for capturing contemporaneous dependencies among financial variables through linear regression and R 2 decomposition. However, we show that it can produce misleading results when causal relationships are present, leading to inconsistencies between the inferred network and the true datagenerating process. To address this issue, we introduce the Directed R 2 connectedness measure, which integrates the LiNGAM algorithm by Shimizu et al. 2006 to uncover structural causal directions. This extension improves both the interpretability and reliability of the connectedness analysis in the presence of underlying causal mechanisms. We validate our framework through simulation studies and apply it to U.S. asset market data, highlighting its advantages over the traditional R 2 approach.

title: Sharing the Algorithm: The Tax Solution to Generative AI

detail.title: Sharing the Algorithm: The Tax Solution to Generative AI

publicationDetails.detailsText: GWU Legal Studies Research Paper Forthcoming

detail.abstract:
This article argues that tax policy offers a core tool for mitigating the sweeping public policy challenges of generative Artificial Intelligence ("AI"). Specifically, we propose a tax that would allow the public to own a share of AI itself, not just through future income tax liabilities or new excise taxes, but a proposed ownership structure that requires a one-time tax payment by generative AI firms in the form of equity.

Fractional public ownership of AI would directly address four of the key harms of AI that have been well-documented in a deep and still expanding literature. First, many types of AI were built through the unauthorized use of millions of copyrighted works, allegedly amounting to copyright infringement on an unprecedented scale. Sharing ownership of AI would compensate injured creators alongside the broader public whose data was nonconsensually harvested. Second, AI is expected to pose massive labor market disruptions, but shared ownership would allow displaced workers to benefit from the profits of the technology substituting for their labor. Third, greater public voice in the corporate governance of AI could lead to greater scrutiny and bolder interventions in the ways AI has been shown to reproduce and compound many existing forms of discrimination. And lastly, sharing the ownership of AI through government’s principal tool for redistribution, taxation, directly addresses the rapid wealth concentration and monopolization already underway with AI developers. This proposal can also work in tandem with targeted regulation of AI and private law remedies to AI’s many harms. 

Ultimately, the original contribution of this paper is to propose a unique in-kind tax payment structure that would require firms with ownership of AI to remit equity shares to the public. The article describes multiple structures for this arrangement, drawing from existing models of fractional ownership used in private investment to serve as a paradigm for a partial public interest in AI. In total, this article argues that many of the greatest concerns related to AI can be solved through sharing AI. And tax policy is the best tool to achieve this goal.

detail.abstract: The global pursuit of decarbonization and net-zero emissions necessitates sustainable and renewable energy alternatives, with biodiesel emerging as a viable solution. This study focuses on utilizing rubber seed oil (RSO), a non-edible and abundant feedstock, for biodiesel production. RSO addresses the dual challenge of reducing reliance on fossil fuels and minimizing competition with food resources. However, the high free fatty acid (FFA) content of RSO presents a significant barrier to efficient biodiesel synthesis through traditional alkaline transesterification. A two-step process, acid esterification followed by alkaline transesterification, was employed to overcome this limitation. The process was optimized using Box-Behnken Design (BBD) within the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) framework. The ideal conditions for maximum biodiesel yield included a methanol-to-oil molar ratio of 5:1, catalyst concentration of 1.19%, reaction time of 79 minutes, and reaction temperature of 61.5°C. Under these parameters, a maximum biodiesel yield of 97.09% was achieved. The resultant biodiesel, rubber seed oil methyl ester (RSOME), was characterized in accordance with ASTM and EN standards. RSOME exhibited superior thermal stability, high flash and fire points, and notable calorific properties, making it a competitive alternative to conventional diesel fuel. By valorizing an underutilized waste resource, this study not only contributes to the advancement of sustainable biodiesel production but also aligns with global decarbonization initiatives. The findings underscore the potential of RSO-derived biodiesel as a critical component of future renewable energy strategies, supporting environmental sustainability and economic viability.

title: Strategic Uncertainty and Sequential Play
affiliations: Indiana University and Indiana University Bloomington, Department of Economics, Students

detail.title: Strategic Uncertainty and Sequential Play
detail.abstract: The paper examines how the timing of decisions shapes outcomes in coordination settings. Theoretically, the outcomes become predictable and efficient when decisions are made sequentially rather than simultaneously. Our experimental evidence shows that sequential moves promote remarkably high efficiency, and these effects are far less sensitive to increased group size. A key finding is that the sequential structure alters the distribution of strategic uncertainty in a group, aggregating it and allocating most of it to the first mover. Dynamic measures further reveal that coordination failures under simultaneous moves stem from weak resilience to setbacks rather than fragility of equilibria.

title: Populist Policymakers
affiliations: Ruhr-University Bochum, Ruhr-University Bochum and Ruhr-Universität Bochum

detail.title: Populist Policymakers
detail.abstract: Populist far-right politicians are increasingly successful across the globe. However, we know little about the personal characteristics of rank-and-file far-right politicians and what part of their success is due to these characteristics. We use hand-collected data on more than 41,000 political candidates for local council elections in the German state of Saxony to study the characteristics and electoral outcomes of Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) politicians. We find that AfD candidates are new entrants to local politics rather than turncoats from other parties. AfD candidates also differ in observable characteristics from candidates of more established parties. However, “characteristics space” demand estimations show that AfD candidates’ electoral success is due to voters’ strong preference for the AfD “party brand”. In fact, voters evaluate (the observed traits of) AfD candidates more negatively than most other parties’ candidates. We decompose the party brand effect into distinct policy dimensions and identify the AfD’s stance on refugees and gender issues as particularly salient to voters.

title: The Specificity Problem: Why Reformed Epistemology Cannot Justify Particular Religious Traditions
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The Specificity Problem: Why Reformed Epistemology Cannot Justify Particular Religious Traditions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This paper was developed in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic), an AI assistant. The author provided the initial philosophical concerns, research question, and core arguments. Claude assisted with structuring the argument, identifying relevant philosophical literature, and refining the presentation. The central thesis regarding the "specificity problem" in Reformed Epistemology and all substantive philosophical claims represent the author's original contribution.

detail.abstract: This paper examines a critical limitation in Alvin Plantinga's Reformed Epistemology: while it may successfully defend generic theistic belief against evidentialist critiques, it fails to justify belief in any particular religious tradition with its specific doctrines and truth claims. Reformed Epistemology argues that belief in God can be "properly basic"-rational without inferential justification-through the operation of the sensus divinitatis, a cognitive faculty that produces theistic beliefs under appropriate circumstances. However, I argue that this mechanism cannot bridge the gap between minimal theism ("something divine exists") and the detailed doctrinal content of Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, or any specific tradition. The sensus divinitatis delivers only generic awareness of transcendence, while particular traditions require acceptance of complex theological propositions about Trinity, prophethood, salvation, scripture, and metaphysics. This "specificity problem" is compounded by three factors: (1) contradictory specific beliefs across traditions cannot all be properly basic, (2) the strong correlation between birthplace and religious belief suggests cultural conditioning rather than basic cognitive response, and (3) appeals to revelation or scripture reintroduce the evidential requirements Reformed Epistemology sought to avoid. I conclude that particular religious traditions lack adequate epistemological justification through properly basic beliefs, leaving intellectually honest inquirers without grounds for choosing one tradition's specific claims over another's.

title: Accounting for Trump Tariffs
affiliations: Florida International University (FIU) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Accounting for Trump Tariffs
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the dramatic surge in US tariffs under the Trump administration in 2025 by quantitatively accounting for its primary drivers. Using a multi-dimensional fixed effects model on monthly data across 231 trading partners, we decompose the total variation in US sectoral tariff rates. Our decomposition reveals a striking hierarchy of motives as the geopolitical targeting of specific countries accounts for 51.5% of the variation, while industrial policy aimed at specific sectors explains an additional 20.5%. In contrast, stable, historical trade patterns account for a mere 12.1%, signaling a radical break from past policy. Our key contribution is this quantitative ranking, showing the geopolitical dimension of the Trump tariffs was more than twice as significant as domestic industrial protectionism. This analysis underscores the significant economic uncertainty generated when trade policy shifts from a rules-based system to one dominated by discretionary bilateral power politics.

title: 'Protected Profit' and Value Sharing to Boost Non-Interfering Investment, Employee Ownership and Democratic Businesses
affiliations: Cardiff University and Cardiff Business School

detail.title: 'Protected Profit' and Value Sharing to Boost Non-Interfering Investment, Employee Ownership and Democratic Businesses
detail.abstract:
Conceptual Paper.

Purpose. Employee ownership (EO) and profit sharing have numerous benefits. Employee Ownership Trusts (EOTs) are proliferating, but EO could grow faster by harnessing ‘non-interfering’, risk-sharing investment. Companies with common ownership (such as EOTs) are at risk, longer-term, from inadequate equity, which could lead to under-investment, slower growth or demutualisation. Other private businesses are also held back by substantial gaps in non-interfering, risk-sharing investment.

Approach. Existing financial instruments do not meet these challenges. We design a viable alternative, balancing the needs of entrepreneurs, workers and investors.

Findings. ‘Protected profit’ sharing between workers and investors achieves this balance: guaranteed ‘base’ pay is capped at a pre-agreed average level; profit-sharing pay and payments to loans, bonds or shares are all agreed fractions of ‘protected profit’ (= revenue – non-pay costs – base pay costs). This aligns interests between workers, entrepreneurs and investors, and together with restricted voting rights, solves the principal-agent/risk-control problems, allowing reward-/risk-sharing equity investment.

Originality. ‘Protected profit’ sharing prevents whoever controls a company from unilaterally raising wages at the expense of investors, while protecting and incentivising everyone in the firm.

Practical implications. Sharing protected profit allows sustainable employee/trust (or entrepreneur) control, while increasing liquidity, reducing the risk of ‘degeneration’, and expanding the range of firms that can transition sustainably to control for/by employees. It also enables private firms in general to attract capital, boosting productivity and growth. 

Social implications. Our mechanism removes the ‘need’ for exorbitant executive pay (a driver of inequality), is compatible with Islamic finance, and will catalyse business, thus civic, democratisation.

title: Designing Causal Experiments in Multiunit Enterprises with a Small Sample and Strategic Agents
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics, The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics and University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business

detail.title: Designing Causal Experiments in Multiunit Enterprises with a Small Sample and Strategic Agents
detail.abstract: Multiunit enterprises increasingly use causal experiments to guide operational decisions. However, their sample sizes are limited; unit heterogeneity undermines matched comparisons; and implementation costs preclude repeated testing. To address these challenges, we propose soliciting counterfactual estimates from unit managers in the treatment group who are better informed about local market conditions but act strategically when incentives are misaligned. We develop a game-theoretic model to examine the impact of experimental design and obtain three surprising insights. First, manager input generally enhances decision quality, but may backfire when incentives are strongly misaligned and the manager's predictive capability is improved. This is because a more capable manager can manipulate the firm's estimation more easily. Second, the relationship between incentive misalignment and decision quality could be non-monotonic: moderate conflicts can cause major distortions, while extreme conflicts may prompt the firm to rationally disregard manager input, reducing its harm. Third, our results are generally consistent with classical theories that favor tightly matched controls; however, in some settings, less well-matched controls can lead to better decisions. When managers have strong predictive capability and a moderate level of incentive misalignment, a better-matched control group reduces their ability to manipulate inference through reported information, thereby incentivizing them to bias the estimation through lowered effort during the experimental stage. Together, these findings overturn the wisdom of classical experimental design. Firms should adopt context-aware experimentation, tailoring both the involvement of managers and treatment assignment strategies to local predictive capability, incentive alignment, and control-group comparability.

title: A Behavioural Study of the Chartered Accountant and Tax Consultant Influence on the Ethics of Individual Taxpayers in India

detail.title: A Behavioural Study of the Chartered Accountant and Tax Consultant Influence on the Ethics of Individual Taxpayers in India
detail.abstract: Tax compliance in India is influenced not only by legal obligations but also by the ethical reasoning of taxpayers and the advisory role of tax professionals. Chartered Accountants (CAs) and tax consultants significantly shape individual taxpayer behaviour by acting as both interpreters of the law and moral influencers. This study investigates how the ethical perspectives of individual taxpayers are affected by their reliance on these professionals. Using a mixed-methods, stakeholder-inclusive approach, the research examines perceptions from taxpayers, tax advisors, and policymakers to explore the behavioural dynamics of ethical tax compliance. The study addresses a gap in existing literature by shifting the focus from institutional models of tax compliance to individual and professional ethics within the advisory ecosystem. It evaluates how tax professionals perceive their ethical obligations, how their guidance affects taxpayer conduct, and how regulatory bodies interpret their role. Findings aim to inform ethical standards, professional training, and tax policy interventions that promote voluntary and ethically grounded tax compliance in India.

title: DVAEFormer: A Denoising Variational AutoEncoder and Transformerbased Framework for Accurate and Robust Remaining Useful Life Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
affiliations: Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology and Nanjing Medical University

detail.title: DVAEFormer: A Denoising Variational AutoEncoder and Transformerbased Framework for Accurate and Robust Remaining Useful Life Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
detail.abstract: As global energy demands escalate, the reliability and longevity of lithium-ion batteries have become paramount in applications such as electric vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and energy regeneration systems. Despite their advantages in size, weight, and energy density, lithium-ion batteries suffer from performance degradation over time, complicating the accurate prediction of their Remaining Useful Life (RUL). Traditional model-based and data-driven approaches face significant challenges, particularly in handling the nonlinear and non-stationary capacity regeneration phenomena and sensitivity to noisy data. This paper introduces DVAEFormer, a novel RUL estimation method that synergistically combines a Denoising Variational AutoEncoder (DVAE) with a Transformer architecture. The proposed model effectively mitigates the capacity regeneration effects by extracting underlying degradation patterns and enhances noise robustness through strategic noise introduction in both input and hidden layers. Additionally, the integration of the Autoencoder with the Transformer optimizes feature extraction and leverages the Transformer's powerful sequence modeling capabilities to improve prediction accuracy and reliability. Comprehensive experiments conducted on benchmark battery datasets demonstrate that DVAEFormer outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness. This study not only advances the methodologies for battery health management but also provides a robust framework for extending the operational lifespan of lithium-ion batteries in critical applications.

title: The Chebyshev Universe: The Mathematical Landscape
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: The Chebyshev Universe: The Mathematical Landscape
detail.abstract: This work establishes a unified analytical framework-the Chebyshev Universethat bridges Pafnuty Lvovich Chebyshev's classical theory of extremal efficiency with contemporary high-dimensional computation. We demonstrate that Chebyshev's foundational principle of optimality under constraint provides the organizing structure for approximation theory, probability, numerical analysis, and tensor computation. Beginning with orthogonal polynomials, minimax approximation, and spectral methods, we establish the numerical stability and exponential convergence properties that render Chebyshev systems indispensable in modern scientific computing. This framework extends naturally to high-dimensional settings through tensor decompositions-Canonical Polyadic, Tucker, Tensor Train, and Hierarchical formats-which preserve orthogonality while achieving polynomial rather than exponential scaling in dimensionality. We derive rigorous approximation bounds for functions with mixed smoothness and demonstrate geometric compression via lowrank tensor manifolds. Applications across quantitative finance, partial differential equations, and climate modeling reveal the practical power of tensorized Chebyshev representations. For rough volatility calibration, we achieve sub-second parameter inference where traditional methods require much more time. For high-dimensional PDEs, exponentially convergent spectral-tensor solvers maintain accuracy with polynomial complexity. We introduce Chebyshev Tensor Networks (CTNs), a novel architecture integrating polynomial spectral expansions with tensor factorizations, achieving sixfold parameter compression with minimal accuracy degradation and near-machine precision on structured problems. The mathematical foundations unify measure theory, WKB asymptotics, and algebraic geometry of tensor varieties. We prove that orthogonality ensures stability through balanced spectral energy, equioscillation guarantees optimality via minimax principles, and tensor rank governs complexity through geometric dimension reduction. These three pillars manifest Chebyshev's overarching principle: true efficiency emerges from structured equilibrium, not from the elimination of error but from its equitable distribution across all degrees of freedom.

title: Rational Bitcoin Exuberance

detail.title: Rational Bitcoin Exuberance
detail.abstract: Systematic Bitcoin variance, aggregate uncertainty, and inflation jointly predict Bitcoin returns and explain the predictive power of cyclical Bitcoin prices, a proxy for Bitcoin risk premia. Contrary to earlier evidence, Bitcoin and equity market returns are strongly correlated in our extended sample. Moreover, the three-factor model exhibits significant explanatory power for equity risk premia, suggesting that crypto-related technological shocks have become a priced source of aggregate risk. Google Trends, a measure of investor attention, forecasts negative returns, but this effect is absorbed by the three factors, challenging behavioral interpretations of Bitcoin's valuation dynamics.

detail.abstract: This report analyzes the legal, institutional, and practical framework for employing third-country nationals (TCNs) in Germany’s live-in care sector. It compares three employment models — direct employment, posting via EU countries, and self-employment — assessing their suitability for TCNs. Empirical findings show that TCNs are willing to work longer hours for lower wages and more frequently take on demanding care situations. title: Expat Run, Expat Driven: To What Extent is the Middle Eastern Economy a By-product of Immigrant Human Capital

detail.title: Expat Run, Expat Driven: To What Extent is the Middle Eastern Economy a By-product of Immigrant Human Capital
detail.abstract: This paper examines the central role expatriate labor has played in shaping the economic development of Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states and, more broadly, the Middle East. While oil revenues remain the foundation of regional prosperity, the study argues that economic diversification and infrastructure growth have been highly dependent on immigrant human capital. Drawing on case evidence from Qatar and the UAE, where expatriates make up over 80% of the workforce, the paper highlights both the contributions of low-skilled labor in construction and services and the knowledge-transfer impact of skilled professionals in technology, health, and education. However, reliance on expatriates has also entrenched social stratification and labor rights challenges. The analysis concludes that expatriate human capital has been indispensable for Middle Eastern growth, but sustainable development requires addressing the vulnerabilities of this labor model.

title: Algorithmic Paradox and Market Integrity: A Critical Analysis of AI-Driven Investment Recommendations in the Colombo Stock Exchange
affiliations: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology

detail.title: Algorithmic Paradox and Market Integrity: A Critical Analysis of AI-Driven Investment Recommendations in the Colombo Stock Exchange
detail.abstract: This article presents the paradoxical nature of investment advice generated by artificial intelligence and its impact on emerging market integrity, using the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) as a case in point. Drawing on an exploratory case study and critical discourse analysis (CDA), the research aims to gain an in-depth understanding of the AI-facilitated stock market issues. The application of the 10Ps iterative research model allows the research to employ a fluid, non-linear method. By comparative analysis of disparate AI-created stock tips and incorporation of fresh scholarly work on algorithmic market manipulation, this study reveals inherent contradictions in AI-informed investment advice systems and proposes a regulatory regime for Sri Lankan capital markets.

title: Tradition With a Global Appetite: The Michelin Guide’s Entry and Evolution in New York City

detail.title: Tradition With a Global Appetite: The Michelin Guide’s Entry and Evolution in New York City
detail.abstract: Research has highlighted that tradition can be beneficial for organizations when it allows them to leverage their past to address new and emerging challenges. However, scholarship has also shown that tradition may act as a detriment to organizational progress when it obfuscates recognition of new opportunities or limits potential actions. This article examines this duality of tradition within the context of the Michelin Guide's 2005 entry into New York City, which marked the first steps outside of Europe in a global expansion of Michelin's restaurant evaluations. Accordingly, this study contributes to our understanding of tradition by disentangling its simultaneously enabling and constraining elements and by providing insights about the strategic malleability of traditionin particular, that organizations may embrace or distance themselves from some elements of their tradition in order to engage with new environments or changing circumstances. Ultimately, this work advances a nuanced perspective about what constitutes organizational tradition, its double-sidedness, and the dynamics of tradition's strategic use.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Good Governance: A Mixed-Methods Analysis of Opportunities and Challenges

detail.title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Good Governance: A Mixed-Methods Analysis of Opportunities and Challenges
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) emerged as a boon in transforming the governance system by implementing the good governance in tangible sense. This study extensively investigates the opacity of intricate of AI in Governance lies in the urgency to demystify the mechanisms of AI models. Specifically, it examines how AI-driven systems enhance decision-making, optimize public service delivery system, and foster citizen participation while addressing ethical concerns (like algorithmic biases, privacy, and accountability). The study employees a mixed-method approach to empirically assess AI's impact on reshaping governance efficiency, public trust, and ethical challenges in India. Study Method: A survey of 350 participants, including government officials (57%) and private sector collaborators (43%), was conducted to evaluate AI's role in governance across key sectors such as public administration, healthcare, and education. Primary outcome measures focused on transparency, efficiency, and accountability metrics. Chi-square tests and descriptive analyses were employed for quantitative data, while thematic analysis was applied to qualitative responses. Findings: Results demonstrated significant consensus on AI's potential to transform governance, particularly in delivery of public services (X² = 24.5, p = 0.002), education (X² = 22.3, p = 0.004), and healthcare (X² = 23.8, p = 0.001) significantly improves accessibility. AI-driven decision-making was widely regarded as a key enabler of efficiency (X² = 18.9, p = 0.000), with strong support for AI-assisted governance rather than full automation. Thus, AI underscores transformative potential for governance system, particularly in enhancing efficiency, innovation and transparency in public service delivery, education, and healthcare sectors. The necessity of human oversight (X² = 20.5, p = 0.000) and robust regulatory frameworks (X² = 22.5, p = 0.000) to address concerns related to algorithmic bias and data privacy risks. Additionally, the study identified transparency and public trust as critical challenges, highlighting the urgent need for context-specific, transparent, and citizencentric approach for AI serves as a force for good governance and equitable public service delivery.

title: Strategic Capital Allocation in Emerging Markets: A Framework for U.S. Corporate Development in High-Growth Frontiers

detail.title: Strategic Capital Allocation in Emerging Markets: A Framework for U.S. Corporate Development in High-Growth Frontiers
detail.abstract: This paper addresses the critical gap in cross-border investment strategies for emerging markets, where 60% of ventures fail despite compelling growth narratives. I introduce an integrated four-phase framework that synthesizes rigorous U.S. corporate development practices with deep, localized operational intelligence gained through direct emerging markets experience. The framework features original tools including a Sector-Attractiveness Matrix, Operational Risk Scorecard, and Scenario-Based Valuation model, demonstrated through a detailed case study of a U.S. MedTech firm's acquisition in Ghana. This research provides practitioners with a replicable playbook to mitigate unique emerging market risks while contributing to academic literature on strategic capital allocation. The findings have significant implications for U.S. competitiveness in high-growth frontiers.

title: Challenges of Village Digitalization Implementation in Indonesia: A Literature Review

detail.title: Challenges of Village Digitalization Implementation in Indonesia: A Literature Review

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no personal or financial interests that could have influenced this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or sensitive personal data and therefore did not require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Village digitalization has become a key agenda in Indonesia's broader digital transformation efforts, aimed at improving public service delivery, strengthening governance, and expanding economic opportunities in rural areas. However, the transition toward digital villages has not been without challenges. This study seeks to identify and analyze the main obstacles in implementing village digitalization through a narrative review of 15 scholarly articles published over the past five years. The findings reveal several recurring challenges: limited telecommunication infrastructure, low levels of digital literacy among rural communities, uneven capacity of village officials, insufficient training and outreach, cultural resistance and persistence of manual practices, weak regulatory frameworks and coordination, as well as constraints in funding and supporting facilities. These factors collectively slow down the progress of digital village initiatives compared to the government's ambitious targets. The study highlights that successful implementation requires a more comprehensive strategy, including infrastructure development, digital literacy programs, clearer regulations, and stronger collaboration among central and local governments, village administrations, the private sector, and community stakeholders.

title: Weaponizing Empathy: A New Paradigm for Negotiating with Authoritarian Regimes

detail.title: Weaponizing Empathy: A New Paradigm for Negotiating with Authoritarian Regimes
detail.abstract:
Despite decades of sanctions, moral condemnation, and coercive diplomacy, authoritarian regimes such as Russia, Iran, and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) have not only endured—they have adapted, consolidated, and, in some cases, expanded their influence. This persistent failure of conventional engagement strategies reveals a paradox: external pressure often reinforces authoritarian resilience rather than undermining it. Rooted in siege narratives and identity politics, these regimes thrive on isolation, using confrontation to legitimize internal control and suppress dissent.

This article introduces a disruptive alternative: tactical empathy—a strategic framework that leverages emotional intelligence, symbolic recognition, and psychological sequencing to engage authoritarian actors on their own terms. Drawing on insights from political psychology and international relations theory, the paper argues that empathy, when deployed tactically, can serve as a Trojan Horse for normative transformation. Far from appeasement, this approach reframes empathy as a calculated instrument of influence, capable of penetrating the emotional architecture of authoritarian legitimacy.

The article develops a five-phase model of “Trojan Horse diplomacy,” encompassing trust-building, selective integration, exposure, elite rewiring, and structural erosion. Through comparative case studies of Russia, Iran, and the DPRK, it demonstrates how empathetic engagement—when sustained, sequenced, and strategically framed—can disrupt authoritarian cohesion and open pathways for gradual democratization. Positioned as a third way between confrontation and appeasement, tactical empathy offers a bold reimagining of diplomatic statecraft in an era of rising autocracy.

title: Capitalism, Commercialism & Culturalism: How can Corporations Profit from Cultural Promotion without Objectifying it?

detail.title: Capitalism, Commercialism & Culturalism: How can Corporations Profit from Cultural Promotion without Objectifying it?
detail.abstract: This paper explores the tension between global capitalism’s drive for profit and the ethical responsibility of corporations engaging with cultural representation. While cultural promotion can enrich brand identity and honor traditions, it often risks appropriation and objectification—reducing cultural symbols to stereotypes for commercial gain. Drawing on theoretical work by Matthes (2019) and Ziff & Rao (1997), the paper illustrates cases of fashion and branding where cultural meaning has been commodified. It then identifies ethical strategies for corporations, including collaboration with cultural representatives and embedding educational storytelling into marketing. The analysis argues that authenticity, respect, and fair partnerships can enable businesses to benefit commercially from cultural promotion while safeguarding cultural integrity. The conclusion emphasizes that ethical cultural engagement increasingly aligns with consumer expectations and enhances corporate reputation alongside profitability.

title: Does Stock Price Crash End Bad-News Hoarding? Evidence from Post-Crash Management Guidance
affiliations: Simon Fraser University, Simon Fraser University (SFU) - Beedie School of Business and Simon Fraser University (SFU) - Beedie School of Business

detail.title: Does Stock Price Crash End Bad-News Hoarding? Evidence from Post-Crash Management Guidance
detail.abstract: Firm-specific stock price crashes are attributed to the sudden release of hidden bad news accumulated over time once it surpasses a critical threshold. We examine whether the crashed firm attempts to offset the crash event by selectively releasing good news while continuing to withhold bad news, or instead it considers the event as an opportunity to reset its disclosure strategies. Using a sample of 769 realized firm-specific crashes matched with non-crashed firms with comparable crash-risk profiles, we find that crashed firms foster the disclosure of remaining bad news and curtail the issuance of good news through management guidance. Investors perceive post-crash bad-news (good-news) disclosures as credible (opportunistic). Overall, our findings indicate that a stock price crash diminishes the marginal benefits of concealing bad news, prompting managers to adopt a more transparent disclosure environment.

title: Optimizing Managed Aquifer Recharge Strategies in the Semi-Arid Alluvial Plain: Using GIS-SMCDA and Sensitivity Analysis Technology
affiliations: Beijing Normal University - Zhuhai Campus, China Institute of Water Resources and Hydropower Research (IWHR) - State Key Laboratory of Simulation and Regulation of Water Cycle in River Basin, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Beijing Normal University - Zhuhai Campus

detail.title: Optimizing Managed Aquifer Recharge Strategies in the Semi-Arid Alluvial Plain: Using GIS-SMCDA and Sensitivity Analysis Technology
detail.abstract: Managed aquifer recharge (MAR) is widely recognized as an effective strategy for sustainable water resource management, capable of mitigating groundwater depletion and supporting the conjunctive use of diverse water sources. However, optimizing recharge methods under complex hydrogeological conditions remains a pivotal challenge. To address this, the present study introduces an integrated MAR zoning optimization framework that combines geographic information system (GIS) analysis, spatial multi-criteria decision analysis (SMCDA), and sensitivity analysis (SA). Six critical hydrogeological indicators—surface elevation, slope, vadose zone lithology, aquifer hydraulic conductivity, recharge resources, and groundwater depth—were systematically identified to assess recharge suitability. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was employed to establish a suitability map specific to MAR zoning. To account for uncertainties and improve robustness in decision-making, a combination of one-factor-at-a-time (OAT) analysis, time-series validation, and simulation of indicator degradation was employed. These approaches ensured more reliable and accurate zoning results. After optimization, the percentage of the area classified as suitable for MAR decreased drastically from 94.59% (≈13,170.38 km²) to 59.57%, representing a 33.87% reduction.. Specifically, suitability for recharge methods such as well injection, infiltration pond, and excess irrigation declined by 9.94%, 11.26%, and 12.67%, respectively, while suitable reaches for check dams experienced a more noticeable reduction of 16.19%. These results not only illuminate the spatial coupling mechanisms between hydrogeological conditions and MAR techniques but also underscore the sensitivity of zoning outcomes to variations in key indicators and analytical weights. By refining the MAR planning process, the proposed framework enhances decision-making reliability and offers a transferable methodology for optimized recharge siting and management. Particularly applicable to water-scarce alluvial plains worldwide.

title: Toward Mixed and Flexible High-Density Parking: Layout Design Optimization under Mixed Autonomy Environment
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Toward Mixed and Flexible High-Density Parking: Layout Design Optimization under Mixed Autonomy Environment
detail.abstract: The limited availability of urban land presents significant challenges for improving parking resource utilization. With the emerging trends of vehicle automation and downsizing, parking systems should adapt to parking patterns across diverse vehicle types. However, existing layout designs focus on maximizing static capacity for homogeneous vehicles, failing to address the heterogeneous and time-varying demand. This study introduces a novel high-density parking (HDP) layout optimization framework that jointly accommodates human-driven vehicles (HDVs), autonomous vehicles (AVs) and autonomous micro vehicles (AMVs) via three space types aligned with vehicle size and automation capability. Using a mixed integer nonlinear programming model, we optimize parking layout to meet actual demand while managing operational complexity, and a flexible layout mechanism enables temporal reconfiguration that responds to time-varying demands. Simulation results demonstrate that the Mixed HDP layout reduces vehicle rejection rates from 47.42% (traditional layout) to 7.38%, while the Flexible Mixed HDP layout further achieves 3.47%. Sensitivity analysis reveals that moderate relocations and reconfiguration transitions provide optimal balance between parking density and operational complexity. Under varying demand scenarios, the framework demonstrates robust adaptability. This research provides insights for upgrading parking facilities under the mixed autonomy environment.

title: Recruiting DEI Labour Forces in an Age of AI-Driven HR: Can Robots Project Biases?

detail.title: Recruiting DEI Labour Forces in an Age of AI-Driven HR: Can Robots Project Biases?
detail.abstract: Over the last few years, artificial intelligence (AI) has become a seamless part of human resources (HR) administration, especially in the area of recruitment. AI-powered technology is more frequently applied to make processes like resume screening, candidate evaluation, and even interviewing candidates easier and more automated. Supporters believe that AI is capable of eliminating human prejudice and fostering Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) by making the recruitment process more objective. Yet, the question is: Can AI tools, with the intent of promoting DEI, still perpetuate biases? This essay discusses how AI-enabled recruitment software can reflect biases and the difficulties involved in creating fair and inclusive systems.

title: A Multi-stage Language Model Post-Training Framework for HVAC Fault Diagnosis in Urban Rail Transit
affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Pennsylvania State University - Penn State, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Zhejiang University

detail.title: A Multi-stage Language Model Post-Training Framework for HVAC Fault Diagnosis in Urban Rail Transit
detail.abstract: Effective fault diagnosis of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems in urban rail transit (URT) stations is vital for ensuring passenger comfort, energy efficiency, and operational reliability. However, the diversity and complexity of these faults tend to increase with system mileage and service time. In response, we construct a fault dataset from textual maintenance records of Ningbo Rail Transit from December 2020 to May 2025, covering 33 equipment categories and over 100 fault types. The dataset poses considerable challenges due to the diversity of fault patterns and the limited detail in the original records, which restricts the effectiveness of the existing diagnostic methods. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-stage post-training framework built on a large language model (LLM). The framework comprises three components: (1) data augmentation via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), (2) supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for cold start, and (3) reinforcement learning based on group relative policy optimization (GRPO). This design enables LLMs to acquire domain-specific knowledge and enhance their reasoning ability. We adopt the Qwen3-0.6B model as the baseline and evaluate performance using both model-based similarity metrics and human-based domain expert evaluations. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with the baseline models, the proposed framework significantly improves both diagnostic accuracy and reasoning quality, achieving a model-based score of 0.768, and human-based evaluations further confirm its practical effectiveness. These results show the transformative and scalable potential of LLM-driven intelligent diagnostics in enhancing the reliability and maintenance efficiency for real-world URT electromechanical systems.

title: Intelligent System Engineering and AI for Uncrewed Commercial Aircraft: Operational Architecture, Technology Readiness, and Strategic Pathways
affiliations: University of Seville and University of Seville

detail.title: Intelligent System Engineering and AI for Uncrewed Commercial Aircraft: Operational Architecture, Technology Readiness, and Strategic Pathways
detail.abstract: This study examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Uncrewed Commercial Aircraft (UCA), reflecting aviation’s drive for efficiency, safety, and scalability. Analysts suggest that partial autonomy in cargo and passenger operations could generate billions in savings by the 2030s, mainly through improved fuel use, predictive maintenance, and higher fleet utilization.  ,The analysis focuses on UCA system architectures, with AI enabling key functions including navigation, detect‑and‑avoid (DAA), remote operation, contingency management, communications, and cybersecurity. System maturity is assessed using Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) alongside a proposed framework of Minimum Acceptable Decision Levels (MADLs), which measures how reliably AI can supplement or replace human decision‑making. Case studies of Xwing, Reliable Robotics, Airbus ATTOL, Dronamics, and Elroy Air illustrate different paths toward autonomy and highlight uneven progress in certification.  ,However, challenges remain pronounced. Certifying machine‑learning tools is difficult because many operate as (“black‑box” models), strengthening the case for Explainable AI. Cybersecurity concerns grow with digital connectivity, while effective human–machine teaming requires interfaces that support situational awareness and operational trust.  ,Most forecasts anticipate a phased trajectory: supervised cargo operations emerging later in the 2020s, regional passenger and broader cargo adoption during the 2030s, and wider autonomous use beyond 2040, contingent on regulatory approval and social acceptance. Successful integration will require harmonized safety standards, robust cyber protection, and transparent public engagement in parallel with technical progress.

title: From ‘Multifaceted Crises’ to ‘Perpetual Uncertainty’: SMEs Navigating the New Normal
affiliations: Cardiff University and Swansea University

detail.title: From ‘Multifaceted Crises’ to ‘Perpetual Uncertainty’: SMEs Navigating the New Normal
detail.abstract: This research builds on the growing body of research on SME resilience to crisis events by aiming to develop a new narrative around ‘perceptual uncertainty’. Previous research has seen crises as isolated, linear, and time-specific events, or ‘multifaceted crises’, however this research highlights that the reality has been very different to this in recent years, with a period of perpetual uncertainty developing since the Covid-19 pandemic of 2020. This research aligns with previous studies by viewing resilience through a resource bricolage lens, seeking to understand how businesses apply their resources to develop resilience, by failing, surviving, or thriving. Using a qualitative methodology, a thematic analysis of 14 interviews with owner-managers of hospitality SMEs in the UK shows that businesses can be resilient to the crises, however the environment of the hospitality sector is increasingly challenging, with perpetual uncertainty apparent through various crisis events that create overlapping and long-lasting issues for businesses. While respondents show the ability to survive through cost-cutting efficiencies to the business, or exploring diversification activities, a more effective aim to overcome the perpetual uncertainty would be to seek a more flexible business model that can adapt to uncertain future challenges.

title: Crash Root-Cause Identification via Trace-Rewarded Causation-Chain Reasoning Large Language Model
affiliations: The Key Laboratory of Road and Traffic Engineering, Ministry of Education, China and Tongji University

detail.title: Crash Root-Cause Identification via Trace-Rewarded Causation-Chain Reasoning Large Language Model
detail.abstract: Road traffic crash is one of the top leading causes of death worldwide. To support the deployment of modern safety improvements such as Highly Automated Driving (HAD), collision analysis requires to reveal crash formation and find the root causes. This study explores Large Language Model (LLM)-based techniques to reconstruct the crash causation chain, and reveal the root causes underlying crash occurrence. By designing trace-reward functions, a domain reasoning model base upon DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B is constructed to identify the root causes. Specifically, the trace-rewards are constructed from accuracy in recognizing crash types and entities, accuracy in extracting crash-related behaviors, and alignment degree of behavior and root cause. Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) is then employed to broaden the exploration of potential root causes and build inference paths. Finally, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) is applied to identify the optimal inference traces through training the model. Empirical analyses are conducted using Multi-Modal Accident Video Understanding (MM-AU) dataset. The results show that the proposed method raises the macro accuracy of root cause identification from 0.427 to 0.870 and improves the macro recall from 0.389 to 0.852. This demonstrates that the proposed method effectively enhances the benchmark model’s ability to understand the process of crash formation. Based on the identified root causes, further analyses and discussions are conducted, providing effective support for traffic safety management and the development of preventive strategies.

title: Rate Allocation Optimization for A Field-scale Edge-water Gas Reservoir in the Sichuan Basin, China: Insights from Streamline-based Mobile Water-gas Ratio​
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Rate Allocation Optimization for A Field-scale Edge-water Gas Reservoir in the Sichuan Basin, China: Insights from Streamline-based Mobile Water-gas Ratio​
detail.abstract: Strong heterogeneity and active aquifer support of most natural gas reservoirs in Sichuan basin, China pose significant challenges for maintaining stable gas production, including early water breakthrough and rapid pressure depletion. Optimal rate allocation is essential for edge-water gas reservoir to maximize gas recovery while controlling water production.This study introduces a novel derivative-free rate allocation optimization method that enhances gas recovery and reduces water production by adjusting well rates based on a streamline-derived mobile water-gas ratio. The entire optimization period is divided into multiple user-defined time intervals, and the process is carried out sequentially. Within each interval, the ratio of mobile water production to gas recovery is calculated at both the well and field levels. These ratios are then used to generate well rate multipliers, which iteratively update the rate allocation. Once an interval is completed, the process moves to the next, continuing until the end of the field life.The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated using a sector model and further validated on a large-scale edge-water gas reservoir in the Sichuan Basin, China. Results indicate that the streamline-based approach successfully optimizes well rates under field constraints, increasing gas recovery while reducing water production. Increasing the gas drainage volume, as represented by time-of-flight to the producer, is identified as a key mechanism for minimizing residual gas.

title: AI production, ethics of personal data privacy, and institutional paradox
affiliations: Howard University

detail.title: AI production, ethics of personal data privacy, and institutional paradox
detail.abstract: As AI algorithms increasingly put surveillance onto the footprints of our daily activities, ethical justification over AI collection, monitoring, and appropriation of personal data becomes an imperative. In this paper, we explore AI professionals’ value ethics perceptions about AI data problem, solutions, and privacy concern to understand the importance of algorithmic personal data demand to institutional operation of supplying (or lack of) personal privacy protection. In respect to AI personal data use, ethical value dilemma is clear. On the one hand, we have societal concern against unwarranted AI surveillance, collection, and use of personal data. On the other hand, the institutional demand for personal data collection can also be ethically justified, given algorithmic reliance upon personal data in maximizing AI functionalities. This study takes up this issue from the standpoint of AI production, with value vacillation between innovation (business) and protection (societal interest), as experienced by industry insiders. We found that ‘privacy paradox’ (high concern, low action) found in consumer behavior also exists in institutional behavior, as institutional beliefs conflict with their data practices, as at the heart of contradiction lie professional demands at the stage of AI production. This study draws upon ethical implications of technical, institutional, and professional demands of algorithmic personal data surveillance, which remains at odds with rising societal concerns regarding AI data use.

title: Restoring Cinematic Realism Through Scene-Level Acoustic Planning (by Austin Shivaji Kumar)
affiliations: Halawi Media Private Limited

detail.title: Restoring Cinematic Realism Through Scene-Level Acoustic Planning (by Austin Shivaji Kumar)

detail.abstract: Bollywood has mastered the visual craft of cinema, yet one dimension of realism remains largely unexplored: acoustics. Most productions still treat sound as a post-process, relying on Foley and artificial reverb to recreate what could have been captured naturally. This paper explores the concept of Scene-Level Acoustic Design: the art and science of predicting how a location will sound before it's even shot. By using room impulse response modeling, acoustic pre-visualization, and coordinated set design, filmmakers can embed realism into sound from the script stage itself. The outcome is not just cleaner audio, but deeper emotional sound that feels like it belongs to the space it's born in.

title: Enhancing Accuracy of Numerical Weather Prediction Models in Road Surface Temperature Forecasting for Winter Road Maintenance Operations in Cold Climate Regions
affiliations: University of Guelph, University of Guelph, University of Guelph, University of Guelph and University of Guelph

detail.title: Enhancing Accuracy of Numerical Weather Prediction Models in Road Surface Temperature Forecasting for Winter Road Maintenance Operations in Cold Climate Regions
detail.abstract: Accurate Road Surface Temperature (RST) forecasting is crucial for effective winter road maintenance and management, especially in cold-climate areas. When pavement temperature is near zero degrees Celsius, one kilogram of salt can melt over 60 kilograms of ice and snow. In contrast, when pavement temperature drops to -10 degrees Celsius, the same kilogram of salt can melt less than 6 kilograms of ice and snow. Therefore, accurate forecasting of pavement temperature on an hourly basis across a road network is a prominent factor for precision salt application to improve road safety and minimize adverse environmental effects. Multiple Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models with high spatial resolution provide hourly RST forecasts with global coverage and are free of charge. In other words, this research forms a core component of a larger road weather management framework that integrates road surface condition modelling and a network of RWIS stations for dynamic, real-time online mapping of the grip (i.e. coefficient of friction) across a road network. The NWP models accurately predict the average surface temperature of a few square kilometres grid area with global coverage. However, NWP model ground surface temperature predictions must be calibrated with deep learning algorithms to match road weather stations' measured road surface temperatures accurately. This study employs advanced machine learning algorithms for correcting systematic biases in RST predictions based on multiple Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models, including BOM_Global, Icon_Global, GFS_HRRR, GFS_Global, GEM_Global, and GEM_HRDPS, for some road weather stations in Canada, Finland, and the USA. Our methodology significantly reduces NWP model RST forecast error (e.g., RMSE from 3.62°C to 0.361°C for GEM_HRDPS in Canada). Moreover, the findings show that among NWP models, GEM_HRDPS and GFS_HRRR were the best for predicting surface temperature in the studied regions. Despite regional variability and computational challenges, combining machine learning with ensemble techniques offers a reliable framework for RST forecasting. These findings provide a foundation for developing operational tools that enhance winter road safety and optimize salt application rates for environmental protection and cost savings for road authorities.

title: Regulatory Inefficacy of Bundling in Platform Fulfillment Services
affiliations: Columbia University - Department of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research (IEOR), Columbia University - Department of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research, University of Florida and Columbia University

detail.title: Regulatory Inefficacy of Bundling in Platform Fulfillment Services
detail.abstract: We propose an economic framework to study  the impact of regulation on bundling behavior whereby a platform (e.g., Amazon) offers a fulfillment service (e.g., Fulfilled by Amazon) and requires merchants to use it for a per-unit fee. Our main finding is that regulations prohibiting such bundling may be ineffective. Specifically, we show that, under regulatory constraints, the platform can restructure pricing to replicate the outcome of bundling. Notably, the platform has discretion to set both a fulfillment service fee and a platform fee. In response to regulation, the platform lowers the fulfillment service fee while raising the platform fee. This deters undercutting by standalone fulfillment service providers and thereby induces merchants to voluntarily use the platform’s fulfillment service. Moreover, the platform fee increase allows the platform to recover profits lost from the reduced fulfillment fee.

title: Status Seeking Taxpayer and Tax Evasion
affiliations: Indian Institute of Foreign Trade,  and

detail.title: Status Seeking Taxpayer and Tax Evasion
detail.abstract: This paper explores whether tax compliance would be affected if the tax payers are “status” seekers. If relative income is a symbol of relative status in a society, status concerned individuals would evade paying taxes more relative to the case where status is not a concern. However, such an outcome would not hold if the symbol of relative status is relative consumption of the “status” good and not relative income. We generalize the scenario by introducing a measure of relative status which depends on both relative income and consumption of the status good.

title: The Post-Circular Economy: How AI Collapses Ideation Costs and Redefines Sustainability From Carbon to Cognition: Accounting for the Green Environment in the Age of AI
affiliations: Anglia Ruskin University

detail.title: The Post-Circular Economy: How AI Collapses Ideation Costs and Redefines Sustainability From Carbon to Cognition: Accounting for the Green Environment in the Age of AI
detail.abstract: The Nordhaus Dynamic Integrated Climate-Economy (DICE) model remains the canonical tool linking growth, emissions, and policy. Yet its exogenous treatment of technological progress fails to capture the transformation now underway, the collapse in the cost of ideation driven by artificial intelligence (AI). This paper integrates Experiential Matrix Theory (EMT) and the Post-Science Paradigm into an augmented DICE framework to model this transition. In this formulation, AI becomes an endogenous ideation engine that couples with human creativity to accelerate decarbonisation and knowledge production, while alignment investment governs whether this acceleration stabilises or destabilises the planet. Sustainability therefore emerges as a function of epistemic speed and ethical alignment. Building on Boulding's (1966) vision of the circular economy, EMT extends circularity beyond material flows to the circulation of intelligence and experience itself. As ideation costs collapse, production increasingly maps in real time onto human experiential needs, enabling a shift from resource-intensive to knowledge-intensive growth. The resulting post-circular economy achieves ecological sufficiency while expanding experiential abundance. Environmental accounting thus evolves from carbon bookkeeping to the management of cognition and alignment, redefining prosperity as the sustainable co-evolution of intelligence, ethics, and experience.

title: Adopting Automated Contracts in Supply Chains: Impact of Execution Lag and Market Uncertainty
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China-School of Management, University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management, Donald G. Costello College of Business at George Mason University and University of Wisconsin - Milwaukee - Sheldon B. Lubar School of Business

detail.title: Adopting Automated Contracts in Supply Chains: Impact of Execution Lag and Market Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Problem definition: Automating contract renegotiation and term updates using generative-AI and blockchain technologies enhance supply chain agility, yet human involvement can create execution lags. Automated contracts with or without lags entail different dynamic interactions. This paper examines: (i) when should supply chains adopt contract automation? (ii) what level of automation should be used? (iii) How should supply chain members design decision rules in automated contracts? Methodology/results: We analyze a game-theoretic model comprising a manufacturer and a retailer in an uncertain market over two periods. In each period, the retailer decides the order quantity after observing a market signal. The manufacturer decides the wholesale price and can automate the contract with or without a lag which differs in available market information. We show that under contract automation, they should discard observed market uncertainty but use its signal to make decisions. We identify an informational effect in the retailer's inventory carryover, which mitigates double marginalization and benefits the supply chain. We characterize the optimal contract type and show that the manufacturer should adopt an automated contract with rather than without lag when the market signal is less informative. Unexpectedly, improved inventory technologies to reduce holding cost and improved forecasting accuracy can lead to lower retailer and supply chain profits due to manufacturer's strategic execution lag. When two symmetric supply chains compete, an asymmetric equilibrium can emerge, with one supply chain adopting automated contract with lag and the other without. Managerial implications: Contract automation's value extends beyond enabling more informed decisions. Manufacturers may strategically use execution lag to incentivize contract automation adoption by the retailer. Supply chains may lose from benevolent technologies in inventory and forecasting, due to endogenous contract automation. Execution lag can be a strategic lever to mitigate supply chain competition.

title: Monetary Policy, Uncertainty, and Communications
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: Monetary Policy, Uncertainty, and Communications

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Boston Working Paper No. 25-11

detail.abstract: We review the design and communication of monetary policy strategies that take into account risks and uncertainty. A key element in a robust monetary strategy is the concept of risk management, which is the weighing of key risks when setting policy. When risks to the outlook are balanced, the baseline outlook may be sufficient to guide policy decisions.  However, risk-management considerations become important when risks are asymmetric. We discuss how robust simple interest rate rules and optimal control policy can incorporate risk-management considerations into the design of a monetary policy strategy. Alternative scenarios can illustrate salient risks and how monetary policy might respond if those risks were to materialize. However, using alternative scenarios in policy deliberations and communications requires important implementation choices.
